\(C_i\), we have \(B_i = B_2^-\). Thus,
by item~(v) of Definition~\ref{def:augmenting} applied to \(S\)
with parameters \(i\) and \(h = 2\),
we have 
\begin{equation} b_0^{i+1} \notin V(\bar B_2- f_2 + e_1 - e_2 + f_3).
\end{equation}
Note that 
\(\bar C_2 = \bar B_2' = \bar B_2- f_2 + e_1\).
Therefore, 
\begin{align} V(\bar B_2- f_2 + e_1 - e_2 + f_3)
	= V(\bar C_2- e_2 + f_3)
	= V(\bar C_2)\cup \{b_0^3\}.
\end{align}
Recall that \(c_0^{i+1} = b_0^{i+1}\) for every \(i\geq 2\). Then, 
by~\eqref{itemiv-a}~and~\eqref{itemiv-b}, 
we have \(c_0^{i+1} \notin V(C_2)\cup\{c_0^3\}\).
\\



\noindent{\textbf{Item (v)}}:  
for \(i=3,\ldots,r-1\) , 
if \(\bar C_i = \bar C_{h}\) for some \(2<h <i\), 


then 
\(c_0^{i+1}\notin V(\bar C_i - f_h^*  + e_{h-1}^* - e_h^*+ f_{h+1}^*)\).\\

Fix $i\in\{3,\ldots,r-1\}$  and suppose that
\(\bar C_i = \bar C_{h}\) for some \(2<h<i\). 

Note that we have \(C_i = C_{h}^-\), and thus \(\bar B_i = \bar B_{h}\) and, 
by Corollary~\ref{cor:augmenting-sequence-repeating-element},
$\bar C_i\neq \bar B_1',\bar B_2'$.
By item~(v) of Definition~\ref{def:augmenting} applied to \(S\), 
we have
\begin{equation} b_0^{i+1} \notin  V(\bar B_h - f_h + e_{h-1}  - e_h + f_{h+1}). 
\end{equation}



Recall that, since \(i\geq 3\), we have $c_0^{i+1} = b_0^{i+1}$, $f_i^* = f_i$ and $e_i^* = e_i$. 
Therefore,  from~\eqref{itemv-a}, we have
\begin{equation*}

c_0^{i+1} \notin  V(\bar C_h - f_h^* + e_{h-1}^*   - e_h^* + f_{h+1}^*). 
\end{equation*}







We concluded the proof that $S'$ is an augmenting sequence of $\mathcal{B}''$. But, since $S$ is a 
full-augmenting sequence of $\mathcal{B}$, we know 
that 
$b^1_0\notin V(B_r)$ (then, clearly $\bar B_r\neq \bar B_1,\bar B_2$). But since 
$c^2_0=b^1_0$, we conclude that $S'$ is a 
full-augmenting sequence of $\mathcal{B}''$.

Since \(|S'| = r-1\), by the induction hypothesis, 
\(G\) admits a $k$-complete \(\ell\)-tracking decomposition \(\mathcal{B}'\)
such that \(\tau(\mathcal{B}') < \tau(\mathcal{B}'') 
\leq \tau(\mathcal{B})\) and $\mathcal{B}'(v) = \mathcal{B}''(v) = \mathcal{B}(v)$
for every vertex $v$ of $G$.
nodes.statement_short: Perform the same swap and show the modified sequence $S'$ is full-augmenting for $\mathcal{B}''$, then apply induction.
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition

nodes.name: Induction hypothesis
nodes.statement:
In the rest of the proof we assume that \(|S| = r> 2\). 
Suppose that the lemma holds when \(\mathcal{B}\) contains a full-augmenting sequence \(S'\)
with length \(r-1\).
nodes.statement_short: Assume $r>2$ and the lemma for sequences of length $r-1$.
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition

nodes.name: Swap first two trackings
nodes.statement:
Since \(|S| > 2\),
by item (ii) of Definition~\ref{def:augmenting} we have
\(b_1^2 = b_{*}^1\)
and \(b_{s(2)}^2=b_0^1\)
where \(s(2) \geq 3\).
Now, consider the trackings $B_1'$ and $B_2'$ that we have
  defined in the proof for the case $|S|=2$. Let $\mathcal{B}''$ be the
  $\ell$-tracking decomposition as we have defined in that case (which we
  called $\mathcal{B}'$), that is, \(\mathcal{B}'' = \mathcal{B} - B_1 - B_2 + B_1' + B_2'\).
  In the case $|S|=2$, we had $b_0^1\notin V(B_2)$, but now we have
  that $b_0^1\in V(B_2)$, thus, in this case we can only conclude that
  \(\tau(\mathcal{B}'') \leq \tau(\mathcal{B})\).  See Figure~\ref{fig:augmenting-a}.
nodes.statement_short: Form $\mathcal{B}''$ by the same swap; now only $\tau(\mathcal{B}'')\le\tau(\mathcal{B})$.
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition

nodes.name: End-counts preserved
nodes.statement:
The next step is to prove that \(\mathcal{B}''(v) = \mathcal{B}(v)\) for all $v\in
V(G)$. The proof follows analogously to the proof we have presented 
for the case $|S|=2$.
nodes.statement_short: End-counts are preserved as in the case $|S|=2$.
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition

nodes.name: B'' is k-complete
nodes.statement:
Now we will prove that \(\mathcal{B}''\) is 
\(k\)-complete. Note that if \(v\neq b_1^2\), then the hanging edges at \(v\)
in \(\mathcal{B}\) are the same hanging edges at \(v\) in \(\mathcal{B}''\).
Now, let \(E_{\mathrm{hang}}(b_1^2)\) be the set of hanging edges at \(b_1^2\) in 
\(\mathcal{B}\).
Then the set of hanging edges at \(b_1^2\) in \(\mathcal{B}''\) is 
\(E_{\mathrm{hang}}(b_1^2)\cup \{b_1^2b_0^2\}\) because 
\(d_{\bar B_1'}(b_0^2) = 1\).
Then, \(\mathrm{hang}(b_1^2,\mathcal{B}'') \geq \mathrm{hang}(b_1^2,\mathcal{B}) > k\).
Therefore, \(\mathcal{B}''\) is \(k\)-complete.
nodes.statement_short: Hanging edges at $b_1^2$ only increase, so $\mathcal{B}''$ is $k$-complete.
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition

nodes.name: Define S'
nodes.statement:
Since $S$ is an augmenting sequence of $\mathcal{B}$, by 
Corollary~\ref{cor:augmenting-sequence-repeating-element}, every $\bar B_i$ 
appears at most twice in $S$ and if 
$\bar B_i=\bar B_j$ for $1\leq i<j\leq r$, 
then, \(B_j = B_i^-\). 
Let \(S' = C_2C_3\cdots C_r\), where, $C_2= B_2'$ and for $3\leq i\leq r$, we have
\[C_i = \begin{cases} 
B_1'^- &\mbox{if } B_i= B_1^-; \\ 

B_2'^- &\mbox{if } B_i= B_2^-; \\ 
B_i & \mbox{otherwise}.\end{cases}\]
nodes.statement_short: Using Corollary 3.3, define $S'=C_2\cdots C_r$ replacing $B_1^-$, $B_2^-$ by $B_1'^-$, $B_2'^-$.
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition

nodes.name: Notation for S'
nodes.statement:
We shall prove that $S'$ is a full-augmenting sequence. For that, we
shall check each of the items of
Definition~\ref{def:augmenting}. Before, we make some observations: we
also denote by $s(i)$ the smallest index such that
$c_0^2 = c_{s(i)}^i=b_0^1$, for $2 \leq i \leq r$.  The vertex $c_j^i$
is the same as $b_j^i$ for $i=3,\ldots,r$ and
$j=0,\ldots,s(i)$.  We denote by $e_i^*$ and $f_i^*$ the edges
  of $C_i$ that correspond to $e_i$ and $f_i$ defined for $B_i$, that
  is, $e_i^*= c_*^ib_0^1$ and $f_i^*=c_0^ic_1^i$.
nodes.statement_short: Plan: verify Definition 3.1 for $S'$; introduce $s(i)$, $e_i^*$, $f_i^*$.
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition

nodes.name: Item (i)
nodes.statement:
\textbf{Item (i)}}: \(\bar C_2\) is not a path, \(d_{\bar
  C_2}(c^2_0) > 1\) and $c^3_0 \notin V(C_2)$. \\

Since $C_2=B_2'$, we have $c^2_0=b^1_0$. Moreover, since 
$\bar B_2'= \bar B_2 - f_2 +e_1$, the edges $e_1$ and $e_2$ are in
$\bar B_2'=C_2$ and are incident to $c_0^2$. Thus, \(d_{\bar C_2}(c^2_0) > 1\).
Now, let us prove
that $c^3_0\notin V(C_2)=V(B_2')$.  Since \(B_2 \neq B_1\),
by item (iii) of Definition~\ref{def:augmenting} (applied to \(S\)
with \(i=2\)),
we have \(b_0^3\notin V(B_2)\).
Since \(b_0^1\in V(B_2)\),
we know that \(V(B'_2)\subset V(B_2)\).
Therefore, \(b_0^3\notin V(B'_2)\).
By the construction of the elements $C_i$, we have \(c_0^3 = b_0^3\),
which implies that \(c_0^3\notin V(B'_2)=V(C_2)\).
nodes.statement_short: $\bar C_2$ is not a path, has degree $>1$ at $c_0^2$, and $c_0^3\notin V(C_2)$.
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition

nodes.name: Item (ii)
nodes.statement:
\textbf{Item (ii)}}: For $i=3,\ldots, r-1$, 
the element \(C_i\) contains \(c_0^2\), and \(c_1^{i} =c^{i-1}_{*}\). \\

Fix \(i\in \{3, \ldots, r\}\). Since $b^1_0\in B_i$, by the definition of $C_i$ 
we have that $c_0^2 = b^1_0\in C_i$.

We shall prove that \(c_1^{i} =c^{i-1}_{*}\). 
(a) If $C_i = B_i$ and $C_{i-1} = B_{i-1}$, then the result follows
by the definition of $C$ and the fact that item (ii) of
Definition~\ref{def:augmenting} holds for the sequence~ $S$.

(b) Suppose $C_i=B_2'^-$.  In this case, $B_i = B_2^-$, and thus
$b_1^i = b_{\ell -1}^2$.  Since $C_i=B_2'^-$, we have that
$c_1^i = b_{\ell-1}^2$.  Combining the equalities
above, we conclude that $c_1^i = b_1^i$.  (b1) If $C_{i-1} = B_{i-1}$
then $c_*^{i-1} = b_*^{i-1}$.  Thus,
$c_1^i =b_1^i = b_*^{i-1} = c_*^{i-1}$ (as the middle equality holds
because item (ii) of Definition~\ref{def:augmenting} holds for $S$).
(b2) If $C_{i-1} \neq B_{i-1}$, then $C_{i-1} = B_1'^-$. The last
equality implies that $c_*^{i-1} = b_{+}^1$ and $B_{i-1} = B_1^-$.
From the last equality, we obtain that $b_*^{i-1} = b_{+}^1$.
Combining the equalities, we get
$c_*^{i-1}= b_{+}^1 =b_*^{i-1} = b_1^i = c_1 ^i$.
 
(c) Suppose $C_i=B_1'^-$. The proof for this case is analogous to the
proof of case (b), interchanging the occurrences of index $2$ and index
$1$. We write the proof for completeness. In this case, $B_i = B_1^-$, and thus
$b_1^i = b_{\ell -1}^1$. Since $C_i=B_1'^-$, we have that
$c_1^i = b_{\ell-1}^1$.  Combining the equalities
above, we conclude that $c_1^i = b_1^i$. (c1) If $C_{i-1} = B_{i-1}$
then $c_*^{i-1} = b_*^{i-1}$.  Thus,
$c_1^i =b_1^i = b_*^{i-1} = c_*^{i-1}$. (c2) If $C_{i-1} \neq B_{i-1}$, then $C_{i-1} = B_2'^-$. The last
equality implies that $c_*^{i-1} = b_{+}^2$ and $B_{i-1} = B_2^-$.
From the last equality, we obtain that $b_*^{i-1} = b_{+}^2$.
Combining the equalities, we get
$c_*^{i-1}= b_{+}^2 =b_*^{i-1} = b_1^i = c_1 ^i$.

(d) Suppose $C_i=B_i$ and $C_{i-1}\neq B_{i-1}$. If $i=3$ then
$C_2=B_2'$, and in this case, $c_1^3=b_1^3 = b_*^2=c_*^2$. If $i>3$,
then $C_{i-1} = B_2'^-$ or $C_{i-1}=B_1'^-$. In both cases, it follows
that $c_*^{i-1} = b_* ^{i-1}$. Then using the fact that $b_1^i=
b_*^{i-1}$ (definition of $S$), it follows that $c_1^i=b_1^i=
b_*^{i-1}=c_*^{i-1}$.
nodes.statement_short: Show $c_1^i=c_*^{i-1}$ by cases on whether $C_i$, $C_{i-1}$ were modified.
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition

nodes.name: Containment of b_0^1
nodes.statement:
Fix \(i\in \{3, \ldots, r\}\). Since $b^1_0\in B_i$, by the definition of $C_i$ 
we have that $c_0^2 = b^1_0\in C_i$.

We shall prove that \(c_1^{i} =c^{i-1}_{*}\).
nodes.statement_short: Each $C_i$ contains $c_0^2=b_0^1$; it remains to show $c_1^i=c_*^{i-1}$.
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition

nodes.name: Case (a)
nodes.statement:
(a) If $C_i = B_i$ and $C_{i-1} = B_{i-1}$, then the result follows
by the definition of $C$ and the fact that item (ii) of
Definition~\ref{def:augmenting} holds for the sequence~ $S$.
nodes.statement_short: Both unmodified: follows from (ii) for $S$.
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition

nodes.name: Case (b)
nodes.statement:
(b) Suppose $C_i=B_2'^-$.  In this case, $B_i = B_2^-$, and thus
$b_1^i = b_{\ell -1}^2$.  Since $C_i=B_2'^-$, we have that
$c_1^i = b_{\ell-1}^2$.  Combining the equalities
above, we conclude that $c_1^i = b_1^i$.  (b1) If $C_{i-1} = B_{i-1}$
then $c_*^{i-1} = b_*^{i-1}$.  Thus,
$c_1^i =b_1^i = b_*^{i-1} = c_*^{i-1}$ (as the middle equality holds
because item (ii) of Definition~\ref{def:augmenting} holds for $S$).
(b2) If $C_{i-1} \neq B_{i-1}$, then $C_{i-1} = B_1'^-$. The last
equality implies that $c_*^{i-1} = b_{+}^1$ and $B_{i-1} = B_1^-$.
From the last equality, we obtain that $b_*^{i-1} = b_{+}^1$.
Combining the equalities, we get
$c_*^{i-1}= b_{+}^1 =b_*^{i-1} = b_1^i = c_1 ^i$.
nodes.statement_short: $C_i=B_2'^-$: chase equalities in subcases (b1), (b2).
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition

nodes.name: Case (c)
nodes.statement:
(c) Suppose $C_i=B_1'^-$. The proof for this case is analogous to the
proof of case (b), interchanging the occurrences of index $2$ and index
$1$. We write the proof for completeness. In this case, $B_i = B_1^-$, and thus
$b_1^i = b_{\ell -1}^1$. Since $C_i=B_1'^-$, we have that
$c_1^i = b_{\ell-1}^1$.  Combining the equalities
above, we conclude that $c_1^i = b_1^i$. (c1) If $C_{i-1} = B_{i-1}$
then $c_*^{i-1} = b_*^{i-1}$.  Thus,
$c_1^i =b_1^i = b_*^{i-1} = c_*^{i-1}$. (c2) If $C_{i-1} \neq B_{i-1}$, then $C_{i-1} = B_2'^-$. The last
equality implies that $c_*^{i-1} = b_{+}^2$ and $B_{i-1} = B_2^-$.
From the last equality, we obtain that $b_*^{i-1} = b_{+}^2$.
Combining the equalities, we get
$c_*^{i-1}= b_{+}^2 =b_*^{i-1} = b_1^i = c_1 ^i$.
nodes.statement_short: $C_i=B_1'^-$: analogous to (b) with indices 1 and 2 swapped.
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition

nodes.name: Case (d)
nodes.statement:
(d) Suppose $C_i=B_i$ and $C_{i-1}\neq B_{i-1}$. If $i=3$ then
$C_2=B_2'$, and in this case, $c_1^3=b_1^3 = b_*^2=c_*^2$. If $i>3$,
then $C_{i-1} = B_2'^-$ or $C_{i-1}=B_1'^-$. In both cases, it follows
that $c_*^{i-1} = b_* ^{i-1}$. Then using the fact that $b_1^i=
b_*^{i-1}$ (definition of $S$), it follows that $c_1^i=b_1^i=
b_*^{i-1}=c_*^{i-1}$.
nodes.statement_short: $C_i$ unmodified, $C_{i-1}$ modified: $c_*^{i-1}=b_*^{i-1}$.
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition

nodes.name: Item (iii)
nodes.statement:
\textbf{Item (iii)}}: For $i=3,\ldots, r-1$,  if
\(\bar C_i \neq \bar C_h\) for every $h<i$,  then $c_0^{i+1} \notin V(C_i)$. \\


Fix $i\in\{3, \ldots, r-1\}$ and suppose \(\bar C_i \neq \bar C_{h}\) 
for every \(2\leq h < i\).

Note that $\bar C_i\neq \bar B_2'$.

First we consider the case where $\bar C_i=\bar B_1'$
or, equivalently, \(C_i = B_1'^-\).
Thus, \(B_i = B_1^-\),
and by item (iv) of Definition~\ref{def:augmenting} applied to \(S\), we have 
\(b_0^{i+1}\notin (V(\bar B_i)\cup\{b_0^2\}) =V(B_1')=V(C_i)\).
Since \(c_0^i = b_0^i\) for every \(i\geq 3\), we have \(c_0^{i+1}\notin 
V(C_i)\).

Now suppose that \(\bar C_i\neq \bar B_1'\).
Then, \(\bar B_i \neq \bar B_1\).
But we know that \(\bar C_i \neq \bar C_{h}\)
for every \( h < i\),
which implies that \(B_i \neq B_{h}\)
for every \(h <i\).
From item (iii) of Definition~\ref{def:augmenting} (applied to \(S\)),
we have that \(b_0^{i+1}\notin V(B_i)\).
Since \(c_0^{i+1}=b_0^{i+1}\),
we have \(c_0^{i+1}\notin V(B_i)\).
Since \(\bar C_i \neq \bar B_1', \bar B_2'\),
we conclude that \(C_i = B_i\), and therefore, \(c_0^{i+1}\notin V(C_i)\).
nodes.statement_short: Verify (iii) for $S'$ separately when $\bar C_i=\bar B_1'$ (via (iv) for $S$) and otherwise (via (iii) for $S$).
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition

nodes.name: Item (iv)
nodes.statement:
\textbf{Item (iv)}}: for \(i=3,\ldots,r-1\) , if 
 \(\bar C_i = \bar C_2\) then \(c_0^{i+1}\notin V(C_i)\cup\{c_0^3\}\).\\

Fix \(i\in\{3,\ldots,r-1\}\) and suppose $\bar C_i= \bar C_2$. In this case, $C_i =B_2'^-$. 
We shall prove that 
$c_0^{i+1}\notin V(B_2')\cup\{c_0^3\}$. Note that, by the definition of 
\(C_i\), we have \(B_i = B_2^-\). Thus,
by item~(v) of Definition~\ref{def:augmenting} applied to \(S\)
with parameters \(i\) and \(h = 2\),
we have 
\begin{equation} b_0^{i+1} \notin V(\bar B_2- f_2 + e_1 - e_2 + f_3).
\end{equation}
Note that 
\(\bar C_2 = \bar B_2' = \bar B_2- f_2 + e_1\).
Therefore, 
\begin{align} V(\bar B_2- f_2 + e_1 - e_2 + f_3)
	= V(\bar C_2- e_2 + f_3)
	= V(\bar C_2)\cup \{b_0^3\}.
\end{align}
Recall that \(c_0^{i+1} = b_0^{i+1}\) for every \(i\geq 2\). Then, 
by~\eqref{itemiv-a}~and~\eqref{itemiv-b}, 
we have \(c_0^{i+1} \notin V(C_2)\cup\{c_0^3\}\).
nodes.statement_short: Verify (iv) for $S'$ using item (v) of $S$ and equations (1)-(2).
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition

nodes.name: Item (v)
nodes.statement:
\textbf{Item (v)}}:  
for \(i=3,\ldots,r-1\) , 
if \(\bar C_i = \bar C_{h}\) for some \(2<h <i\), 


then 
\(c_0^{i+1}\notin V(\bar C_i - f_h^*  + e_{h-1}^* - e_h^*+ f_{h+1}^*)\).\\

Fix $i\in\{3,\ldots,r-1\}$  and suppose that
\(\bar C_i = \bar C_{h}\) for some \(2<h<i\). 

Note that we have \(C_i = C_{h}^-\), and thus \(\bar B_i = \bar B_{h}\) and, 
by Corollary~\ref{cor:augmenting-sequence-repeating-element},
$\bar C_i\neq \bar B_1',\bar B_2'$.
By item~(v) of Definition~\ref{def:augmenting} applied to \(S\), 
we have
\begin{equation} b_0^{i+1} \notin  V(\bar B_h - f_h + e_{h-1}  - e_h + f_{h+1}). 
\end{equation}



Recall that, since \(i\geq 3\), we have $c_0^{i+1} = b_0^{i+1}$, $f_i^* = f_i$ and $e_i^* = e_i$. 
Therefore,  from~\eqref{itemv-a}, we have
\begin{equation*}

c_0^{i+1} \notin  V(\bar C_h - f_h^* + e_{h-1}^*   - e_h^* + f_{h+1}^*). 
\end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Verify (v) for $S'$ from item (v) of $S$, equation (3).
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition

nodes.name: S' is full-augmenting
nodes.statement:
We concluded the proof that $S'$ is an augmenting sequence of $\mathcal{B}''$. But, since $S$ is a 
full-augmenting sequence of $\mathcal{B}$, we know 
that 
$b^1_0\notin V(B_r)$ (then, clearly $\bar B_r\neq \bar B_1,\bar B_2$). But since 
$c^2_0=b^1_0$, we conclude that $S'$ is a 
full-augmenting sequence of $\mathcal{B}''$.
nodes.statement_short: Since $c_0^2=b_0^1\notin V(B_r)$, $S'$ is full-augmenting.
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition

nodes.name: Apply induction
nodes.statement:
Since \(|S'| = r-1\), by the induction hypothesis, 
\(G\) admits a $k$-complete \(\ell\)-tracking decomposition \(\mathcal{B}'\)
such that \(\tau(\mathcal{B}') < \tau(\mathcal{B}'') 
\leq \tau(\mathcal{B})\) and $\mathcal{B}'(v) = \mathcal{B}''(v) = \mathcal{B}(v)$
for every vertex $v$ of $G$.
nodes.statement_short: Induction on $S'$ gives the required $\mathcal{B}'$.
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition

nodes.name: End-counts preserved by the swap (|S|=2)
nodes.statement: \(\mathcal{B}'(v) = \mathcal{B}(v)\) for every \(v\in V(G)\).
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 3.5
nodes.statement:
Given $v\in V(G)$ and a set 
$\mathcal{T}\subset \mathcal{B}$, define $\mathcal{B}_{odd}|_\mathcal{T}(v)$ as the number of 
elements \(B\in\mathcal{T}\) such that 
\(d_{\bar B}(v)\) is odd, and define $\mathcal{B}_{even}|_\mathcal{T}$ as the number of 
elements \(B=x_0\cdots x_{\ell}\) of 
\(\mathcal{T}\) such that $x_0=x_\ell=v$. Furthermore, let
$\mathcal{B}|_\mathcal{T}(v)=\mathcal{B}_{odd}|_\mathcal{T}(v) + 
2\mathcal{B}_{even}|_\mathcal{T}(v)$.

























Let $B_{\mathop{\text{\rm vert}}\nolimits}=\{b_0^1,b_0^2,b_1^2\}$. Clearly, 
$\mathcal{B}(v)=\mathcal{B}'(v)$ for every $v\notin 
B_{\mathop{\text{\rm vert}}\nolimits}$. Let $\mathcal{T}=\{B_1,B_2\}$ and
$\mathcal{T'}=\{B_1',B_2'\}$ .
To prove that  $\mathcal{B}(v)=\mathcal{B}'(v)$ 
holds also for vertices $v\in B_{\mathop{\text{\rm vert}}\nolimits}$, it is enough to show that 
$\mathcal{B}|_{\mathcal{T}}(v)=\mathcal{B}'|_{\mathcal{T'}}(v)$, because we already know that 
$\mathcal{B}|_{\mathcal{B}\setminus\mathcal{T}}(v)=\mathcal{B}'|_{\mathcal{B}'\setminus\mathcal{T'}}(v)$. 
Recall that $\mathcal{B}|_{\mathcal{T}}(v)$
$\big($resp. $\mathcal{B}'|_{\mathcal{T'}}(v) \big)$ is the number 
edges of \(G\) that are starting edges of elements in \(\mathcal{T}\) $\big($resp. \(\mathcal{T'}\)$\big)$ that 
start at \(v\), or ending edges of elements in \(\mathcal{T}\) $\big($
resp. \(\mathcal{T'}\)$\big)$ that end at 
\(v\).  First, note that
$\mathcal{B}|_{\mathcal{T}}(b_0^1)=\mathcal{B}'|_{\mathcal{T'}}(b_0^1)$.  Indeed, the
edge $f_1=b_0^1b_1^1$ is the starting edge of $B_1$, but it is not a
starting edge of neither $B_1'$ or $B_2'$; but, on the other hand, the
starting edge of $B_2'$ starts at $b_0^1$. Thus, the number of
starting edges that starts at $b_0^1$ is the same in $\mathcal{B}$ and in
$\mathcal{B}'$. In terms of ending edges that end at $b_0^1$, the same happens:
if $e_1=b_*^1b_0^1$ is and ending edge of $B_1$, then the
ending edge of $B_1'$ (which is the reverse of $f_1$) also ends at
$b_0^1$, and if  $e_1$ is not an ending edge of $B_1$, then neither $B_1'$ or $B_2'$ has an ending edge incident to $b_0^1$. 
It is easy to see that
$\mathcal{B}|_{\mathcal{T}}(b_1^2)=\mathcal{B}'|_{\mathcal{T'}}(b_1^2)$, as $b_1^2$ is
an internal vertex of all trackings under analysis. Also,
$\mathcal{B}|_{\mathcal{T}}(b_0^2)=\mathcal{B}'|_{\mathcal{T'}}(b_0^2)$, as  the
starting edge $f_2= b_0^2b_1^2$ of $B_2$ becomes the starting edge of
$B_1'$, and no other change occurs in terms of ending edges at
$b_0^2$.
nodes.statement_short: Localize $\mathcal{B}(v)$ to the two swapped trackings and check the three affected vertices $b_0^1,b_0^2,b_1^2$.
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition

nodes.name: Restricted counts
nodes.statement:
Given $v\in V(G)$ and a set 
$\mathcal{T}\subset \mathcal{B}$, define $\mathcal{B}_{odd}|_\mathcal{T}(v)$ as the number of 
elements \(B\in\mathcal{T}\) such that 
\(d_{\bar B}(v)\) is odd, and define $\mathcal{B}_{even}|_\mathcal{T}$ as the number of 
elements \(B=x_0\cdots x_{\ell}\) of 
\(\mathcal{T}\) such that $x_0=x_\ell=v$. Furthermore, let
$\mathcal{B}|_\mathcal{T}(v)=\mathcal{B}_{odd}|_\mathcal{T}(v) + 
2\mathcal{B}_{even}|_\mathcal{T}(v)$.
nodes.statement_short: Define the counts $\mathcal{B}|_\mathcal{T}(v)$ restricted to a subfamily.
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition

nodes.name: Only three vertices change
nodes.statement_short: Counts can only change at $b_0^1,b_0^2,b_1^2$.
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition

nodes.name: Reduce to swapped pair
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathcal{T}=\{B_1,B_2\}$ and
$\mathcal{T'}=\{B_1',B_2'\}$ .
To prove that  $\mathcal{B}(v)=\mathcal{B}'(v)$ 
holds also for vertices $v\in B_{\mathop{\text{\rm vert}}\nolimits}$, it is enough to show that 
$\mathcal{B}|_{\mathcal{T}}(v)=\mathcal{B}'|_{\mathcal{T'}}(v)$, because we already know that 
$\mathcal{B}|_{\mathcal{B}\setminus\mathcal{T}}(v)=\mathcal{B}'|_{\mathcal{B}'\setminus\mathcal{T'}}(v)$.
nodes.statement_short: It suffices to compare counts on $\{B_1,B_2\}$ and $\{B_1',B_2'\}$.
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition

nodes.name: Recall meaning
nodes.statement:
Recall that $\mathcal{B}|_{\mathcal{T}}(v)$
$\big($resp. $\mathcal{B}'|_{\mathcal{T'}}(v) \big)$ is the number 
edges of \(G\) that are starting edges of elements in \(\mathcal{T}\) $\big($resp. \(\mathcal{T'}\)$\big)$ that 
start at \(v\), or ending edges of elements in \(\mathcal{T}\) $\big($
resp. \(\mathcal{T'}\)$\big)$ that end at 
\(v\).
nodes.statement_short: Recall the counts are numbers of starting/ending edges at $v$.
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition

nodes.name: Vertex b_0^1 and b_1^2
nodes.statement:
First, note that
$\mathcal{B}|_{\mathcal{T}}(b_0^1)=\mathcal{B}'|_{\mathcal{T'}}(b_0^1)$.  Indeed, the
edge $f_1=b_0^1b_1^1$ is the starting edge of $B_1$, but it is not a
starting edge of neither $B_1'$ or $B_2'$; but, on the other hand, the
starting edge of $B_2'$ starts at $b_0^1$. Thus, the number of
starting edges that starts at $b_0^1$ is the same in $\mathcal{B}$ and in
$\mathcal{B}'$. In terms of ending edges that end at $b_0^1$, the same happens:
if $e_1=b_*^1b_0^1$ is and ending edge of $B_1$, then the
ending edge of $B_1'$ (which is the reverse of $f_1$) also ends at
$b_0^1$, and if  $e_1$ is not an ending edge of $B_1$, then neither $B_1'$ or $B_2'$ has an ending edge incident to $b_0^1$. 
It is easy to see that
$\mathcal{B}|_{\mathcal{T}}(b_1^2)=\mathcal{B}'|_{\mathcal{T'}}(b_1^2)$, as $b_1^2$ is
an internal vertex of all trackings under analysis.
nodes.statement_short: Starting and ending edges at $b_0^1$ are exchanged one for one; $b_1^2$ is internal throughout.
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition

nodes.name: Vertex b_0^2
nodes.statement:
Also,
$\mathcal{B}|_{\mathcal{T}}(b_0^2)=\mathcal{B}'|_{\mathcal{T'}}(b_0^2)$, as  the
starting edge $f_2= b_0^2b_1^2$ of $B_2$ becomes the starting edge of
$B_1'$, and no other change occurs in terms of ending edges at
$b_0^2$.
nodes.statement_short: At $b_0^2$, $f_2$ becomes the starting edge of $B_1'$.
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition

nodes.name: Completeness preserved by the swap (|S|=2)
nodes.statement: \(\mathcal{B}'\) is \(k\)-complete.
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 3.6
nodes.statement:
Let us prove that \(\mathrm{hang}(v,\mathcal{B}')>k\) for every $v\in V(G)$.
Note that if \(v\neq b_1^2\), then the hanging edges at \(v\)
in \(\mathcal{B}'\) are the same hanging edges at \(v\) in \(\mathcal{B}\).
Let \(E_{\mathrm{hang}}\) be the set of hanging edges at \(b_1^2\) in \(\mathcal{B}\).
 Since $d_{\bar B_1}(b_0^1) > 1$ (by Definition~\ref{def:augmenting} (i1)), we know that 
\(e_1=b_0^1b_{*}^1=b_0^1b_1^2 \notin E_{\mathrm{hang}}\).
The set of hanging edges at \(b_1^2\) in \(\mathcal{B}'\) is \(E_{\mathrm{hang}}\cup 
\{b_0^1b_1^2, b_0^2b_1^2\}\) because 
\(d_{\bar B_1'}(b_0^2) = 1\) and \(d_{\bar B_2'}(b_0^1) = 1\).
Then, \(\mathrm{hang}(b_1^2,\mathcal{B}') >  \mathrm{hang}(b_1^2,\mathcal{B})  > k \).
Therefore, \(\mathcal{B}'\) is \(k\)-complete.
nodes.statement_short: Only hanging edges at $b_1^2$ change, and the swap adds two hanging edges there.
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition

nodes.name: Only b_1^2 changes
nodes.statement:
Let us prove that \(\mathrm{hang}(v,\mathcal{B}')>k\) for every $v\in V(G)$.
Note that if \(v\neq b_1^2\), then the hanging edges at \(v\)
in \(\mathcal{B}'\) are the same hanging edges at \(v\) in \(\mathcal{B}\).
nodes.statement_short: Hanging edges are unchanged except at $b_1^2$.
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition

nodes.name: e_1 not hanging
nodes.statement:
Let \(E_{\mathrm{hang}}\) be the set of hanging edges at \(b_1^2\) in \(\mathcal{B}\).
 Since $d_{\bar B_1}(b_0^1) > 1$ (by Definition~\ref{def:augmenting} (i1)), we know that 
\(e_1=b_0^1b_{*}^1=b_0^1b_1^2 \notin E_{\mathrm{hang}}\).
nodes.statement_short: By (i1), $e_1$ was not a hanging edge at $b_1^2$.
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition

nodes.name: New hanging edges
nodes.statement:
The set of hanging edges at \(b_1^2\) in \(\mathcal{B}'\) is \(E_{\mathrm{hang}}\cup 
\{b_0^1b_1^2, b_0^2b_1^2\}\) because 
\(d_{\bar B_1'}(b_0^2) = 1\) and \(d_{\bar B_2'}(b_0^1) = 1\).
nodes.statement_short: $\mathcal{B}'$ gains the hanging edges $b_0^1b_1^2$ and $b_0^2b_1^2$.
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement:
Then, \(\mathrm{hang}(b_1^2,\mathcal{B}') >  \mathrm{hang}(b_1^2,\mathcal{B})  > k \).
Therefore, \(\mathcal{B}'\) is \(k\)-complete.
nodes.statement_short: Hence $\mathrm{hang}(b_1^2,\mathcal{B}')>k$.
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition

nodes.name: Item (v) of S applied at h=2
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition
nodes.label: itemiv-a

nodes.name: Vertex set of the modified trail C_2
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition
nodes.label: itemiv-b

nodes.name: Item (v) of S applied at h
nodes.statement: b_0^{i+1} \notin  V(\bar B_h - f_h + e_{h-1}  - e_h + f_{h+1}).
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition
nodes.label: itemv-a

nodes.name: Feasible tracking decomposition
nodes.statement:
Let \(\ell\) be a positive integer.
Let \(G\) be a graph and  \(\mathcal{B}\) be an \(\ell\)-tracking decomposition of \(G\).
We say that \(\mathcal{B}\) is \emph{feasible} if for every \(v\in V(G)\) the
following holds: if \(T\) is a 
vanilla $\ell$-trail of $G$ (not necessarily in \(\mathcal{B}\)) that contains \(v\) as an internal vertex, then 
there exists a hanging edge \(vw\) at \(v\) in $\mathcal{B}$ 
such that \(w\notin V(T)\).
nodes.statement_short: Every vanilla $\ell$-trail through $v$ as an internal vertex misses the far end of some hanging edge at $v$.
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition

nodes.name: Completeness implies feasibility in bipartite graphs
nodes.statement:
Let \(\ell\) and \(k\) be a positive integers and \(G\) be a bipartite graph. 
If \(k\geq \lceil (\ell +1)/2\rceil\) and 
\(\mathcal{B}\) is an \(k\)-complete \(\ell\)-tracking decomposition of \(G\),
then \(\mathcal{B}\) is feasible.
assumptions: Let \(\ell\) and \(k\) be a positive integers and \(G\) be a bipartite graph.
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition
nodes.label: lemma:choose-element-all

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.8
nodes.statement:
Let $\ell$, \(k\), $G$ and $\mathcal{B}$ be as in the hypothesis
  of the lemma. 
   Fix $v\in V(G)$ and suppose \(T\)
  is a vanilla $\ell$-trail of $G$ that contains \(v\).
  Since \(\mathcal{B}\)
  is \(k\)-complete,
  $\mathrm{hang}(v,\mathcal{B})> k$.  Let
  \(vw_1,\ldots,vw_{k+1}\)
  be hanging edges at $v$ in $\mathcal{B}$.
	
	
	We claim that there exists an index \(1\leq i\leq k+1\) 
	such that \(w_i \notin V(T)\). 	Let \(W = \{w_1,\ldots,w_{k+1}\}\).
	Let $G=(A,B;E)$ and suppose, without loss of generality, that \(v\in A\).
	Since \(G\) is bipartite, \(W\subset B\). Furthermore, since \(T\) 
contains at most \(\ell + 1\) 
	vertices, \(|V(T)\cap B| \leq  \lceil (\ell+1)/2\rceil \leq k\). But since 
$|W|=k+1$, we 
	conclude that there exists a vertex $w\in W$ such that \(w\notin V(T)\).
nodes.statement_short: Pigeonhole: $k+1$ hanging neighbours of $v$ lie on the other side, but a trail has at most $\lceil(\ell+1)/2\rceil\le k$ vertices there.
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition

nodes.name: Fix v and T
nodes.statement:
Let $\ell$, \(k\), $G$ and $\mathcal{B}$ be as in the hypothesis
  of the lemma. 
   Fix $v\in V(G)$ and suppose \(T\)
  is a vanilla $\ell$-trail of $G$ that contains \(v\).
nodes.statement_short: Fix $v$ and a vanilla trail $T$ through $v$.
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition

nodes.name: k+1 hanging edges
nodes.statement:
Since \(\mathcal{B}\)
  is \(k\)-complete,
  $\mathrm{hang}(v,\mathcal{B})> k$.  Let
  \(vw_1,\ldots,vw_{k+1}\)
  be hanging edges at $v$ in $\mathcal{B}$.
nodes.statement_short: $k$-completeness gives hanging edges $vw_1,\dots,vw_{k+1}$.
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition

nodes.name: Some w_i avoids T
nodes.statement:
We claim that there exists an index \(1\leq i\leq k+1\) 
	such that \(w_i \notin V(T)\). 	Let \(W = \{w_1,\ldots,w_{k+1}\}\).
	Let $G=(A,B;E)$ and suppose, without loss of generality, that \(v\in A\).
	Since \(G\) is bipartite, \(W\subset B\). Furthermore, since \(T\) 
contains at most \(\ell + 1\) 
	vertices, \(|V(T)\cap B| \leq  \lceil (\ell+1)/2\rceil \leq k\). But since 
$|W|=k+1$, we 
	conclude that there exists a vertex $w\in W$ such that \(w\notin V(T)\).
nodes.statement_short: Some $w_i\notin V(T)$, by counting on the bipartition.
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition

nodes.name: Set W
nodes.statement:
Let \(W = \{w_1,\ldots,w_{k+1}\}\).
	Let $G=(A,B;E)$ and suppose, without loss of generality, that \(v\in A\).
	Since \(G\) is bipartite, \(W\subset B\).
nodes.statement_short: Let $W$ be the far ends; WLOG $v\in A$, so $W\subset B$.
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition

nodes.name: Pigeonhole
nodes.statement:
Furthermore, since \(T\) 
contains at most \(\ell + 1\) 
	vertices, \(|V(T)\cap B| \leq  \lceil (\ell+1)/2\rceil \leq k\). But since 
$|W|=k+1$, we 
	conclude that there exists a vertex $w\in W$ such that \(w\notin V(T)\).
nodes.statement_short: $|V(T)\cap B|\le k<|W|$.
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition

nodes.name: Existence of full-augmenting sequences
nodes.statement:
Let \(\ell\) be a positive integer, \(G\) be a graph and 
	 \(\mathcal{B}\) be an \(\ell\)-tracking decomposition of $G$. If $\mathcal{B}$ is
         feasible and \(\tau(\mathcal{B}) > 0\),
	then \(\mathcal{B}\) contains a full-augmenting sequence.
assumptions:
Let \(\ell\) be a positive integer, \(G\) be a graph and 
	 \(\mathcal{B}\) be an \(\ell\)-tracking decomposition of $G$
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition
nodes.label: lemma:existence-of-sequence

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3.9
nodes.statement:
Let \(\ell\), \(G\) and $\mathcal{B}$ be as in the hypothesis of the lemma. 	
	First, let us show that \(\mathcal{B}\) contains an augmenting sequence.
	Since \(\tau(\mathcal{B}) > 0\), 
	the tracking decomposition \(\mathcal{B}\) contains a tracking \(B_1\) 
	that does not induce a path.

Let $B_1 = b_0^1b_1^1\cdots b_\ell^1$, where $d_{\bar B_1}(b^1_0)>1$. 



	


	Since \(\mathcal{B}\) is feasible, there is a hanging edge \(b_{*}^1w\) 
	at (the internal vertex) \(b_{*}^1\) in \(\mathcal{B}\) such that \(w\notin V(B_1)\).
	Let \(B_2\) be the element of \(\mathcal{B}\) that contains the edge \(b_{*}^1w\).
	Then, it is easy to verify that \(B_1B_2\) is an augmenting sequence of $\mathcal{B}$.
	
	Let \(S=B_1B_2\cdots B_r\) be a maximal augmenting sequence of $\mathcal{B}$.
	Suppose by contradiction that \(S\) is not a full-augmenting sequence, i.e, \(b_0^1 \in V(B_r)\).


	

	Now we show how to obtain an element \(B_{r+1}\) of $B$ such that 
$S'=B_1\cdots B_rB_{r+1}$ is an augmenting sequence, contradicting the maximality 
of $S$. 
Since \(S\) is an augmenting sequence, item (i1) of Definition~\ref{def:augmenting} holds,
and items (ii)--(v) of Definition~\ref{def:augmenting} hold for \(i=1,\ldots,r-1\).
Since \(S\) is not a full-augmenting sequence, \(B_r\) contains \(b_0^1\).
Our aim is to find an element \(B_{r+1}\) for which
items (iii)--(v) of Definition~\ref{def:augmenting} hold for \(i=r\).
Before continuing, note that \(b_*^i\) is a vertex of \(B_i\)
in the tracking \(P_i = b_1^ib_2^i\cdots b_{*}^i\), and
therefore \(b_*^i\) is always an internal vertex of \(B_i\) 
(because \(B_i\) contains the tracking \(P_i b_0^1\)).
Now, note that exactly one of the following holds: 
(a)~\(\bar B_r \neq \bar B_h\), for every \(h<r\);
(b)~\(\bar B_r = \bar B_1\); or
(c)~\(\bar B_r = \bar B_h\) for some \(1 < h < r\).



\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] 


	In this case, by the feasibility of \(\mathcal{B}\), considering \(T=\bar B_r\)
	and \(v=b_{*}^r\), 
	there exists a hanging edge \(b_{*}^rz\) at \(b_{*}^r\) such that \(z\notin V(B_r)\).
	Let \(B_{r+1}\) be the element of \(\mathcal{B}\) containing \(b_{*}^rz\).
	We can suppose without loss of generality that \(z=b_0^{r+1}\)
	(otherwise, \(z = b_\ell^{r+1}\) and we choose \(B_{r+1}^-\) instead of \(B_{r+1}\)).
	Then, \(b_1^{r+1} = b_*^{r}\), \(b_0^{r+1} = z \notin V(B_r)\), and

\item[(b)]  



	In this case, we have \(B_r = B_1^-=b^1_\ell P_r b^1_0 P_1^-b_0^1\).

	(note that \(T\) is induced by the tracking \(b_\ell^1P_rb_0^1P_1b_0^2\)),

that \(z\notin V(T)\).
	Note that \(V(T) = V(B_1)\cup\{b_0^2\}\).
	Let \(B_{r+1}\) be the element of \(\mathcal{B}\) containing 
\(b_{*}^rz\).
	As in the previous case, we may assume that \(z = b_0^{r+1} \notin V(B_r)\cup\{b_0^2\}\).

	item (iv) of Definition~\ref{def:augmenting} holds for \(i=r\).

Definition~\ref{def:augmenting}, $b_1^{h}=b^{h-1}_{*}$ 
	and $b_1^{h+1}=b^{h}_{*}$. Then, since 
$b^{h-1}_{s(h-1)}=b^{h}_{s(h)}=b^1_0$, we conclude that 
	$e_{h-1}=b_1^{h}b_0^1$ and $f_{h+1}=b_{*}^{h}b_0^{h+1}$ are edges of 
\(B_{h-1}\) and \(B_{h+1}\), respectively.
	Put \(T = \bar B_r - b_1^{h}b_0^{h} + b_1^{h}b_0^1 
	- b_{*}^{h}b_0^1 + b_{*}^{h}b_0^{h+1} 
	= \bar B_r - f_h + e_{h-1} 
	- e_h + f_{h+1}\)
	(note that \(T\) is induced by the tracking \(b_\ell^hP_rb_0^1P_hb_0^{h+1}\)).
















	Since $T$ is a vanilla $\ell$-trail, by the feasibility of \(\mathcal{B}\), considering
	\(v=b_{*}^r\) and \(T\), 
	there is a hanging edge \(b_{*}^rz\) at \(b_{*}^r\) such 
that \(z\notin V(T)\).
	Let \(B_{r+1}\) be the element of \(\mathcal{B}\) containing 
\(b_{*}^rz\).
	As in the previous case, we may assume that \(z = b_0^{r+1} \notin V(T)\).


	Then, \(b_1^{r+1} = b_*^{r}\) and 
	item (v) of Definition~\ref{def:augmenting} holds for \(i=r\).
\end{itemize}










	




	
	We just proved that there exists an element $B_{r+1}$ of $\mathcal{B}$ 
such that $S'=B_1B_2\cdots B_r B_{r+1}$ is 
	an augmenting sequence of \(\mathcal{B}\),
	a contradiction to the maximality of \(S\). 
	Therefore, \(S\) is a full-augmenting sequence.

nodes.name: An augmenting sequence exists
nodes.statement:

	Let \(B_2\) be the element of \(\mathcal{B}\) that contains the edge \(b_{*}^1w\).
	Then, it is easy to verify that \(B_1B_2\) is an augmenting sequence of $\mathcal{B}$.

nodes.name: Improvement step for feasible complete tracking decompositions
assumptions: Let \(\ell\) be a positive integer and let \(G\) be a graph.
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition
nodes.label: cor:main

nodes.name: The Disentangling Lemma
nodes.statement:
Let \(\ell\) and $k$ be positive integers and let \(G\) be a bipartite graph.
	If $k\geq \lceil (\ell +1)/2\rceil$ and $\mathcal{B}$ is a $k$-complete 
	\(\ell\)-tracking decomposition of $G$,
	then \(G\) admits a $k$-complete
	\(\ell\)-path tracking decomposition \(\mathcal{B}'\)
	such that \(\mathcal{B}'(v) = \mathcal{B}(v)\) for every vertex \(v\) of \(G\).
assumptions: Let \(\ell\) and $k$ be positive integers and let \(G\) be a bipartite graph.
conclusions:
\(G\) admits a $k$-complete
	\(\ell\)-path tracking decomposition \(\mathcal{B}'\)
	such that \(\mathcal{B}'(v) = \mathcal{B}(v)\) for every vertex \(v\) of \(G\)
nodes.statement_short: In a bipartite graph, a $k$-complete $\ell$-tracking decomposition with $k\ge\lceil(\ell+1)/2\rceil$ can be turned into a $k$-complete $\ell$-path decomposition with the same end-counts.
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition
nodes.label: lemma:disentangling

nodes.name: Proof of the Disentangling Lemma
nodes.statement:
Let \(\ell\), \(k\), \(G\) and  $\mathcal{B}$ be as in the hypothesis of the lemma. 

Let \(\mathbb{B}\) be the set of all \(k\)-complete 
\(\ell\)-tracking decompositions \(\mathcal{B}'\) of \(G\)
such that \(\mathcal{B}'(v) = \mathcal{B}(v)\) for every vertex \(v\) of \(G\).
By the hypothesis, \(\mathbb{B} \neq \emptyset\).
Let \(\tau^* = \min\{\tau(\mathcal{B}') \colon \mathcal{B}' \in \mathbb{B}\}\) 
and let \(\mathcal{B}_{\min}\) be an element of \(\mathbb{B}\) such that \(\tau(\mathcal{B}_{\min}) = \tau^*\).
If \(\tau^* = 0\), then \(\mathcal{B}_{\min}\) is an \(\ell\)-path tracking decomposition 
and the proof is complete. 
Then, assume \(\tau^*>0\).

By Lemma~\ref{lemma:choose-element-all},
\(\mathcal{B}_{\min}\) is a feasible \(\ell\)-tracking decomposition.
Since \(\tau(\mathcal{B}_{\min})>0\), by Corollary~\ref{cor:main}
(applied with \(k\), $\ell$, $G$ and $\mathcal{B}_{\min}$), 
there exists an $k$-complete \(\ell\)-tracking decomposition $\mathcal{B}'$ 
of $G$ such that \(\tau(\mathcal{B}') < \tau(\mathcal{B}_{\min}) = \tau^*\) and \(\mathcal{B}'(v) = \mathcal{B}(v)\) for every 
vertex \(v\) of \(G\). 
Therefore, $\mathcal{B}'$ is an element of $\mathbb{B}$ with $\tau(\mathcal{B}') < \tau(\mathcal{B}_{\min})$, 
a contradiction to the minimality of \(\tau^*\).
nodes.statement_short: Take a decomposition minimizing $\tau$ among $k$-complete ones with the same end-counts; if $\tau>0$, Lemma 3.8 and Corollary 3.10 give a smaller one.
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition

nodes.name: Family of decompositions
nodes.statement:
Let \(\ell\), \(k\), \(G\) and  $\mathcal{B}$ be as in the hypothesis of the lemma. 

Let \(\mathbb{B}\) be the set of all \(k\)-complete 
\(\ell\)-tracking decompositions \(\mathcal{B}'\) of \(G\)
such that \(\mathcal{B}'(v) = \mathcal{B}(v)\) for every vertex \(v\) of \(G\).
By the hypothesis, \(\mathbb{B} \neq \emptyset\).
nodes.statement_short: Let $\mathbb{B}$ be the nonempty set of admissible decompositions.
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition

nodes.name: Minimal tau
nodes.statement:
Let \(\tau^* = \min\{\tau(\mathcal{B}') \colon \mathcal{B}' \in \mathbb{B}\}\) 
and let \(\mathcal{B}_{\min}\) be an element of \(\mathbb{B}\) such that \(\tau(\mathcal{B}_{\min}) = \tau^*\).
If \(\tau^* = 0\), then \(\mathcal{B}_{\min}\) is an \(\ell\)-path tracking decomposition 
and the proof is complete. 
Then, assume \(\tau^*>0\).
nodes.statement_short: Take $\mathcal{B}_{\min}$ minimizing $\tau$; done if $\tau^*=0$, else assume $\tau^*>0$.
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition

nodes.name: Feasible and improvable
nodes.statement:
By Lemma~\ref{lemma:choose-element-all},
\(\mathcal{B}_{\min}\) is a feasible \(\ell\)-tracking decomposition.
Since \(\tau(\mathcal{B}_{\min})>0\), by Corollary~\ref{cor:main}
(applied with \(k\), $\ell$, $G$ and $\mathcal{B}_{\min}$), 
there exists an $k$-complete \(\ell\)-tracking decomposition $\mathcal{B}'$ 
of $G$ such that \(\tau(\mathcal{B}') < \tau(\mathcal{B}_{\min}) = \tau^*\) and \(\mathcal{B}'(v) = \mathcal{B}(v)\) for every 
vertex \(v\) of \(G\).
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 3.8 makes $\mathcal{B}_{\min}$ feasible; Corollary 3.10 gives smaller $\tau$.
nodes.section: 3.2 Hanging edges and complete tracking decomposition

nodes.name: Contradiction
nodes.statement:
Therefore, $\mathcal{B}'$ is an element of $\mathbb{B}$ with $\tau(\mathcal{B}') < \tau(\mathcal{B}_{\min})$, 
a contradiction to the minimality of \(\tau^*\).
nodes.statement_short: This contradicts the minimality of $\tau^*$.
