\(\mathcal{B}\).
Therefore \(\mathcal{B}(x_0) \geq d_{F_{1,k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(x_0) + d_{M_2}(x_0)\), from where 
we conclude that
\(\mathcal{B}(v) = d_{F_{1,k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(v) + d_{M_2}(v)\) for every \(v\) in \(A_1\).
Thus, for every vertex \(v\) in \(A_1\) we have 
\[
	\mathcal{B}(v)	= d_{F_{1,k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(v) + d_{M_2}(v)
			= d^*(v) + d_{M_2}(v)
			= d_{G_1}(v)/(2k+1) + d_{M_2}(v).
\]
Analogously, we have \(\mathcal{B}(v) = d_{G_2}(v)/(2k+1) + d_{M_1}(v)\)
for each vertex \(v\) in \(A_2\).
Thus, \(\mathcal{B}\) is an \(\mathbb{F}\)-balanced $(2k+1)$-tracking decomposition.
nodes.statement_short: Two-sided count: end-edges at $x_0$ come exactly from the $S_{x_1}$ sets, giving equality with the balance formula.
nodes.section: 5 Decomposition into paths of odd length

nodes.name: Upper bound
nodes.statement:
Fix \(x_0\in A_1\). First we will prove that  \(\mathcal{B}(x_0) \leq 
d_{F_{1,k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(x_0) + d_{M_2}(x_0)\). If there is no tracking \(T = 
x_0x_1\cdots x_{2k+1}\) in \(\mathcal{B}\),
where \(x_0x_1\) is an edge of \(E(G) - E(G')\), then $\mathcal{B}(x_0)=0$. 
For every such tracking $T$, by the construction of $\mathcal{B}$, we know that \(x_0x_1\) is an 
element of \(S_{x_1}\).
Since \(x_1\) is a vertex of \(A_2\), we have \(S_{x_1} \subset M_2\cup 
F_{1,k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}\).
Therefore,
\begin{equation*}
\mathcal{B}(x_0) \leq d_{F_{1,k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(x_0) + d_{M_2}(x_0).
\end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Every end-edge at $x_0$ lies in an $S_{x_1}$, bounding $\mathcal{B}(x_0)$ above.
nodes.section: 5 Decomposition into paths of odd length

nodes.name: Lower bound
nodes.statement:
Now we will prove that \(\mathcal{B}(x_0) \geq d_{F_{1,k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(x_0) + 
d_{M_2}(x_0)\). Note that, if \(x_0x_1\) is an edge of \(M_2\cup 
F_{1,k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}\)
that is incident to \(x_0\) in \(A_1\) \big(these are the only edges of $G$ that 
can contribute to $\mathcal{B}(x_0)$\big), 
then, by the construction of $\mathcal{B}$, there is a tracking \(Q' = x_1\cdots x_{2k}\) in 
\(\mathcal{B}'\) of a path
such that the tracking \(Q = x_0x_1\cdots x_{2k+1}\) (of a vanilla trail) belongs to 
\(\mathcal{B}\).
Therefore \(\mathcal{B}(x_0) \geq d_{F_{1,k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(x_0) + d_{M_2}(x_0)\), from where 
we conclude that
\(\mathcal{B}(v) = d_{F_{1,k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(v) + d_{M_2}(v)\) for every \(v\) in \(A_1\).
nodes.statement_short: Every such edge is an end-edge of an extended tracking.
nodes.section: 5 Decomposition into paths of odd length

nodes.name: Balance
nodes.statement:
Thus, for every vertex \(v\) in \(A_1\) we have 
\[
	\mathcal{B}(v)	= d_{F_{1,k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(v) + d_{M_2}(v)
			= d^*(v) + d_{M_2}(v)
			= d_{G_1}(v)/(2k+1) + d_{M_2}(v).
\]
Analogously, we have \(\mathcal{B}(v) = d_{G_2}(v)/(2k+1) + d_{M_1}(v)\)
for each vertex \(v\) in \(A_2\).
Thus, \(\mathcal{B}\) is an \(\mathbb{F}\)-balanced $(2k+1)$-tracking decomposition.
nodes.statement_short: Substitute $d^*$ to obtain the balance formula on both sides.
nodes.section: 5 Decomposition into paths of odd length

nodes.name: Extended decomposition is pre-complete (odd case)
nodes.statement: \(\mathcal{B}\) is \((2k+1)\)-pre-complete.
nodes.section: 5 Decomposition into paths of odd length

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 5.9
nodes.statement:
Let \(v\in A_i\). We shall prove that \(\mathrm{preHang}(v,\mathcal{B}) > 2k+1\).
Note that, by the construction of $\mathcal{B}$, the set of pre-hanging edges at \(v\) in 
\(\mathcal{B}\) is exactly \(S_v\).
Then, \(\mathrm{preHang}(v,\mathcal{B}) = |S_v| = \mathcal{B}'(v)\).
Since \(\mathcal{B}'\) is balanced, \(\mathcal{B}'(v) \geq d_{G'_i}(v)/(2k-1)\).
Therefore,
\begin{equation*}
	\mathrm{preHang}(v,\mathcal{B})	= \mathcal{B}'(v) 
					\geq d_{G'_i}(v)/(2k-1) 
					= d^*(v) 
					= d_{G_i}(v)/(2k+1).
\end{equation*} 
Since \(\mathbb{F}\) is a strong \((1,2k+1)\)-bifactorization of \(G\),
we have \(d_{G_i}(v) \geq (2k+1)(2k+2)\), from where we conclude that 
\(\mathrm{preHang}(v,\mathcal{B}) \geq 2k+2\).
Therefore, \(\mathcal{B}\) is a \((2k+1)\)-pre-complete tracking decomposition.
nodes.statement_short: Pre-hanging edges at $v$ are exactly $S_v$, whose size is bounded below via balance and strongness.
nodes.section: 5 Decomposition into paths of odd length

nodes.name: Goal
nodes.statement: Let \(v\in A_i\). We shall prove that \(\mathrm{preHang}(v,\mathcal{B}) > 2k+1\).
nodes.statement_short: Fix $v\in A_i$; show $\mathrm{preHang}(v,\mathcal{B})$ is large.
nodes.section: 5 Decomposition into paths of odd length

nodes.name: preHang = |S_v|
nodes.statement:
Note that, by the construction of $\mathcal{B}$, the set of pre-hanging edges at \(v\) in 
\(\mathcal{B}\) is exactly \(S_v\).
Then, \(\mathrm{preHang}(v,\mathcal{B}) = |S_v| = \mathcal{B}'(v)\).
nodes.statement_short: Pre-hanging edges at $v$ are exactly $S_v$.
nodes.section: 5 Decomposition into paths of odd length

nodes.name: Lower bound
nodes.statement:
Since \(\mathcal{B}'\) is balanced, \(\mathcal{B}'(v) \geq d_{G'_i}(v)/(2k-1)\).
Therefore,
\begin{equation*}
	\mathrm{preHang}(v,\mathcal{B})	= \mathcal{B}'(v) 
					\geq d_{G'_i}(v)/(2k-1) 
					= d^*(v) 
					= d_{G_i}(v)/(2k+1).
\end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Balance of $\mathcal{B}'$ bounds $\mathrm{preHang}(v,\mathcal{B})$ below by a multiple of $d^*(v)$.
nodes.section: 5 Decomposition into paths of odd length

nodes.name: Strongness
nodes.statement:
Since \(\mathbb{F}\) is a strong \((1,2k+1)\)-bifactorization of \(G\),
we have \(d_{G_i}(v) \geq (2k+1)(2k+2)\), from where we conclude that 
\(\mathrm{preHang}(v,\mathcal{B}) \geq 2k+2\).
Therefore, \(\mathcal{B}\) is a \((2k+1)\)-pre-complete tracking decomposition.
nodes.statement_short: Strongness gives the required bound.
nodes.section: 5 Decomposition into paths of odd length

nodes.name: F-balanced tracking decomposition (even case)
nodes.statement:
Let \(k\) be a positive integer.
Let \(G = (A,B;E)\) be a bipartite graph 
that admits a \(\big(2,2(2k+2)\big)\)-bifactorization 
\(\mathbb{F}=(\mathcal{F}_1,\mathcal{F}_2)\),
and let \(G_i = G\big[\bigcup_{F\in\mathcal{F}_i}F\big]\) for \(i=1,2\).
Let \(M_1,N_1\) be the \(\big(A,1,2(2k+2)\big)\)-factors of \(\mathbb{F}\) and 
\(M_2,N_2\) be the
\(\big(B,1,2(2k+2)\big)\)-factors of \(\mathbb{F}\).

We say that a \((2k+2)\)-tracking decomposition \(\mathcal{B}\) of $G$ into is
\emph{\(\mathbb{F}\)-balanced} if the following holds.
	\begin{itemize}
		\item \(\mathcal{B}(v) = d_{G_1}(v)/(2k+2) + d_{M_2}(v)
			+ d_{N_2}(v)\) for every \(v\in A\);
		\item \(\mathcal{B}(v) = d_{G_2}(v)/(2k+2) + d_{M_1}(v)
			+ d_{N_1}(v)\) for every \(v\in B\).
	\end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: A $(2k+2)$-tracking decomposition whose end-counts are $d_{G_1}(v)/(2k+2)+d_{M_2}(v)+d_{N_2}(v)$ on $A$ and symmetrically on $B$.
nodes.section: 6 Decomposition into paths of even length

nodes.name: Balanced 2-path decomposition from a (2,4)-bifactorization
nodes.statement:
If \(G\) is a bipartite graph that admits a 
	\((2,4)\)-bifactorization~\(\mathbb{F}\),
	then \(G\) admits an \(\mathbb{F}\)-balanced $2$-path decomposition.
assumptions:
\(G\) is a bipartite graph that admits a 
	\((2,4)\)-bifactorization~\(\mathbb{F}\)
nodes.section: 6 Decomposition into paths of even length
nodes.label: lemma:2-PD

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 6.2
nodes.statement:
Let \(G = (A,B;E)\) be a bipartite graph 
	that admits a \((2,4)\)-bifactorization
	\(\mathbb{F} = (\mathcal{F}_1,\mathcal{F}_2)\) and put \(\mathcal{F}_i 
= 
\{M_i,N_i,F_i\}\) for \(i = 1,2\).
	Let \(O_{F_i}\) be an Eulerian orientation of \(G[F_i]\), for \(i = 1,2\).
	Let \(\mathcal{C}_1\) be the set of components of \(G[F_1]\).
	Let \(T\) be an element of \(\mathcal{C}_1\) and \(B_T = a_0b_0a_1b_1\cdots a_sb_s\) 
	be a tracking of \(T\), where \(a_i \in A\), and \(b_i \in B\), for \(1\leq i\leq s\).
	We have that \(\mathcal{B}'_T = \{a_ib_ia_{i+1}\colon 0\leq i\leq s\}\),
	taking \(a_{s+1} = a_0\), is a \(2\)-tracking decomposition of \(T\)
	in which every tracking has its end-vertices in \(A\).
	Therefore, \(\mathcal{B}'_1 = \cup_{T\in\mathcal{C}_1}\mathcal{B}'_T\) is a 
	\(2\)-tracking decomposition of \(G[F_1]\) in which every tracking has its end-vertices in \(A\).




	Analogously \(G[F_2]\) admits a \(2\)-tracking decomposition \(\mathcal{B}'_2\) in which every tracking
	has its end-vertices in \(B\).






	Let \(v\) be a vertex in \(A\).
	Since \(M_1\) and \(N_1\) are \((1,1,4)\)-factors of \(G\) we have \(d_{M_1}(v) = d_{N_1}(v)\).
	Thus, the number of edges in \(M_1\cup N_1\) incident to \(v\) is even,
	and we can decompose the edges in \(M_1\cup N_1\) incident to \(v\) 
	into \(2\)-paths such that each path has its end-vertices in \(B\).
	Taking any tracking of each of these paths, we obtain a \(2\)-tracking decomposition \(\mathcal{B}''_1\) 
	of the edges in \(M_1\cup N_1\) 
	such that each path has its end-vertices in \(B\).
	Analogously, there is a \(2\)-tracking decomposition \(\mathcal{B}''_2\) of the edges in \(M_2\cup N_2\) 
	such that each path has its end-vertices in \(A\).


	
	Let \(\mathcal{B} = \mathcal{B}'_1\cup\mathcal{B}'_2\cup\mathcal{B}''_1\cup\mathcal{B}''_2\).
	Note that only the paths in \(\mathcal{B}'_1\) and in \(\mathcal{B}''_2\) have end-vertices
	in~\(A\),
	and analogously
	only the paths in \(\mathcal{B}'_2\) and in \(\mathcal{B}''_1\) have end-vertices in \(B\).
	Therefore, if \(v\) is a vertex of \(A\), 
	then \(\mathcal{B}(v) = \mathcal{B}'_1(v) + \mathcal{B}''_2(v) 
		= d_G(v)/2 + d_{M_2}(v) + d_{N_2}(v)\),
	and	if \(v\) is a vertex of \(B\), 
	then \(\mathcal{B}(v) = \mathcal{B}'_2(v) + \mathcal{B}''_2(v) 
		= d_G(v)/2 + d_{M_1}(v) + d_{N_1}(v)\).
	Thus, \(\mathcal{B}\) is an \(\mathbb{F}\)-balanced $2$-path tracking decomposition of \(G\).
nodes.statement_short: Split the Eulerian factors into 2-paths ending in $A$ (resp. $B$) and pair the two matchings at each vertex into 2-paths; count ends.
nodes.section: 6 Decomposition into paths of even length

nodes.name: 2-paths in G[F_1]
nodes.statement:
Let \(G = (A,B;E)\) be a bipartite graph 
	that admits a \((2,4)\)-bifactorization
	\(\mathbb{F} = (\mathcal{F}_1,\mathcal{F}_2)\) and put \(\mathcal{F}_i 
= 
\{M_i,N_i,F_i\}\) for \(i = 1,2\).
	Let \(O_{F_i}\) be an Eulerian orientation of \(G[F_i]\), for \(i = 1,2\).
	Let \(\mathcal{C}_1\) be the set of components of \(G[F_1]\).
	Let \(T\) be an element of \(\mathcal{C}_1\) and \(B_T = a_0b_0a_1b_1\cdots a_sb_s\) 
	be a tracking of \(T\), where \(a_i \in A\), and \(b_i \in B\), for \(1\leq i\leq s\).
	We have that \(\mathcal{B}'_T = \{a_ib_ia_{i+1}\colon 0\leq i\leq s\}\),
	taking \(a_{s+1} = a_0\), is a \(2\)-tracking decomposition of \(T\)
	in which every tracking has its end-vertices in \(A\).
	Therefore, \(\mathcal{B}'_1 = \cup_{T\in\mathcal{C}_1}\mathcal{B}'_T\) is a 
	\(2\)-tracking decomposition of \(G[F_1]\) in which every tracking has its end-vertices in \(A\).
nodes.statement_short: Cut closed trackings of $G[F_1]$ into 2-trackings with ends in $A$.
nodes.section: 6 Decomposition into paths of even length

nodes.name: Same for G[F_2]
nodes.statement:
Analogously \(G[F_2]\) admits a \(2\)-tracking decomposition \(\mathcal{B}'_2\) in which every tracking
	has its end-vertices in \(B\).
nodes.statement_short: Symmetrically for $G[F_2]$ with ends in $B$.
nodes.section: 6 Decomposition into paths of even length

nodes.name: Pair matching edges
nodes.statement:
Let \(v\) be a vertex in \(A\).
	Since \(M_1\) and \(N_1\) are \((1,1,4)\)-factors of \(G\) we have \(d_{M_1}(v) = d_{N_1}(v)\).
	Thus, the number of edges in \(M_1\cup N_1\) incident to \(v\) is even,
	and we can decompose the edges in \(M_1\cup N_1\) incident to \(v\) 
	into \(2\)-paths such that each path has its end-vertices in \(B\).
	Taking any tracking of each of these paths, we obtain a \(2\)-tracking decomposition \(\mathcal{B}''_1\) 
	of the edges in \(M_1\cup N_1\) 
	such that each path has its end-vertices in \(B\).
	Analogously, there is a \(2\)-tracking decomposition \(\mathcal{B}''_2\) of the edges in \(M_2\cup N_2\) 
	such that each path has its end-vertices in \(A\).
nodes.statement_short: Pair $M_1$ and $N_1$ edges at each $v\in A$ into 2-paths with ends in $B$, and symmetrically.
nodes.section: 6 Decomposition into paths of even length

nodes.name: Balanced
nodes.statement:
Let \(\mathcal{B} = \mathcal{B}'_1\cup\mathcal{B}'_2\cup\mathcal{B}''_1\cup\mathcal{B}''_2\).
	Note that only the paths in \(\mathcal{B}'_1\) and in \(\mathcal{B}''_2\) have end-vertices
	in~\(A\),
	and analogously
	only the paths in \(\mathcal{B}'_2\) and in \(\mathcal{B}''_1\) have end-vertices in \(B\).
	Therefore, if \(v\) is a vertex of \(A\), 
	then \(\mathcal{B}(v) = \mathcal{B}'_1(v) + \mathcal{B}''_2(v) 
		= d_G(v)/2 + d_{M_2}(v) + d_{N_2}(v)\),
	and	if \(v\) is a vertex of \(B\), 
	then \(\mathcal{B}(v) = \mathcal{B}'_2(v) + \mathcal{B}''_2(v) 
		= d_G(v)/2 + d_{M_1}(v) + d_{N_1}(v)\).
	Thus, \(\mathcal{B}\) is an \(\mathbb{F}\)-balanced $2$-path tracking decomposition of \(G\).
nodes.statement_short: Count path ends to verify balance.
nodes.section: 6 Decomposition into paths of even length

nodes.name: Pre-completeness gives completeness (even case)
nodes.statement:
Let \(k\) be a positive integer.
	Let \(G\) be a bipartite graph that admits a  
	\(\big(2,2(2k+2)\big)\)-bifactorization \(\mathbb{F}\).
	If \(G\) admits an \(\mathbb{F}\)-balanced \((2k+3)\)-pre-complete $(2k+2)$-tracking decomposition, 
	then \(G\) admits an \(\mathbb{F}\)-balanced \((k+2)\)-complete $(2k+2)$-tracking decomposition.
assumptions:
Let \(G\) be a bipartite graph that admits a  
	\(\big(2,2(2k+2)\big)\)-bifactorization \(\mathbb{F}\)
nodes.section: 6 Decomposition into paths of even length
nodes.label: lemma:even-complete

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 6.3
nodes.statement:
Let \(k\) be a positive integer.
	Let \(G = (A,B;E)\) be a bipartite graph that admits a 
	\((2,2(2k+2))\)-bifactorization \(\mathbb{F}\).
	Let $\mathcal{F}$ be the set of all \(\mathbb{F}\)-balanced 
	\((2k+3)\)-pre-complete $(2k+2)$-tracking decompositions of $G$. 
	Now let \(\mathcal{B}\) be a tracking decomposition in $\mathcal{F}$ 
	such that  \(\sum_{v\in V(G)} \mathrm{hang}(v,\mathcal{B})\) is maximum over all 
	tracking decompositions in $\mathcal{F}$.
	We claim that \(\mathcal{B}\) is a \((k+2)\)-complete tracking decomposition,
	i.e, \(\mathrm{hang}(v,\mathcal{B}) > k+2\) for each vertex \(v\) of \(G\).
	
	Suppose, for a contradiction, that \(\mathcal{B}\) is not \((k+2)\)-complete.
	Then there is a vertex \(v\) of \(G\) such that \(\mathrm{hang}(v,\mathcal{B}) \leq k+2\).
	Suppose, without loss of generality, that \(v\) is a vertex of \(A\).
	Since \(\mathcal{B}\) is \((2k+3)\)-pre-complete, \(\mathrm{preHang}(v,\mathcal{B}) \geq 2k+4\).
	Thus, there are at least \(k+2\) pre-hanging edges at \(v\) 
	that are not hanging edges at \(v\), say \(x_1v,\ldots,x_{k+2}v\).
	Let \(T_1 = y_0y_1\cdots y_{2k+2}\) be the element of \(\mathcal{B}\) that contains \(x_1v\),
	where, without loss of generality, \(y_0 = x_1\) and \(y_1 = v\).
	The vertices of \(T_1\) in \(B\) are \(y_0,y_2,\ldots, y_{2k+2}\).
	First, we will show that for some $x_i\notin V(T_1)$ for some \(2\leq i \leq k+2\). 
	
	Since \(y_2\) is in \(B\) and \(y_0\) is the end-vertex of \(T_1\) in \(B\), 
	the vertex \(y_2\) is not an end-vertex of \(T_1\). 
	Since \(y_1y_2 \in E(T_1)\), the edge \(y_1y_2\) is not a pre-hanging edge at \(v\).
	Then, \(y_2 \neq x_i\) for every \(2\leq i\leq k+2\). 
	Therefore, \(|\{y_4, y_6,\ldots,y_{2k+2}\}| = k\) and \(|\{2,\ldots,k+2\}| = k+1\), 
	from where we conclude that for at least one \(i\), we have \(x_i \notin V(T_1)\).
	
	Now let \(T_i = z_0z_1\cdots z_{2k+2}\) be the element of \(\mathcal{B}\) that contains \(x_iv\).
	Suppose, without loss of generality, that \(z_1 = v\) and \(z_0 = x_i\).
	Let \(T'_1 = vy_1\cdots y_{2k+1}\) and \(T'_i = y_0 z_1\cdots z_{2k+2}\)
	and let \(\mathcal{B}' = \mathcal{B} - T_1 - T_i + T'_1 + T'_i\).
	We note that \(\bar T'_1 = \bar T_1 - x_1v + x_iv\) and \(\bar T'_i = \bar T_i -x_iv + x_1v\).
	Since \(x_i \notin V(T_1)\), we have \(d_{T'_1}(x_i) = 1\), which 
implies that \(x_iv\) is a hanging edge of \(\mathcal{B}'\) at \(v\).
	Therefore, \(\sum_{v\in V(G)} \mathrm{hang}(v,\mathcal{B}') > 
			\sum_{v\in V(G)} \mathrm{hang}(v,\mathcal{B})\).
			
	We claim that \(\mathcal{B}'\) is \(\mathbb{F}\)-balanced.
	Indeed, since the set of pre-hanging edges at~\(v\) is the same in 
\(\mathcal{B}\) and \(\mathcal{B}'\),
	we have \(\mathcal{B}(v) = \mathcal{B}'(v)\) for every \(v\) in \(V(G)\).
	Therefore, \(\mathcal{B}'\) is an \(\mathbb{F}\)-balanced 
\((2k+3)\)-pre-complete
	decomposition such that 
	\(\sum_{v\in V(G)} \mathrm{hang}(v,\mathcal{B}') > 
			\sum_{v\in V(G)} \mathrm{hang}(v,\mathcal{B})\),
	a contradiction to the choice of \(\mathcal{B}\).
nodes.statement_short: Extremal choice: take a balanced pre-complete decomposition maximizing the number of hanging edges; a vertex with too few hanging edges allows an edge swap that increases it.
nodes.section: 6 Decomposition into paths of even length

nodes.name: Extremal decomposition
nodes.statement:
Let \(k\) be a positive integer.
	Let \(G = (A,B;E)\) be a bipartite graph that admits a 
	\((2,2(2k+2))\)-bifactorization \(\mathbb{F}\).
	Let $\mathcal{F}$ be the set of all \(\mathbb{F}\)-balanced 
	\((2k+3)\)-pre-complete $(2k+2)$-tracking decompositions of $G$. 
	Now let \(\mathcal{B}\) be a tracking decomposition in $\mathcal{F}$ 
	such that  \(\sum_{v\in V(G)} \mathrm{hang}(v,\mathcal{B})\) is maximum over all 
	tracking decompositions in $\mathcal{F}$.
nodes.statement_short: Choose $\mathcal{B}$ maximizing the total number of hanging edges.
nodes.section: 6 Decomposition into paths of even length

nodes.name: Claim completeness
nodes.statement:
We claim that \(\mathcal{B}\) is a \((k+2)\)-complete tracking decomposition,
	i.e, \(\mathrm{hang}(v,\mathcal{B}) > k+2\) for each vertex \(v\) of \(G\).
nodes.statement_short: Claim: $\mathcal{B}$ is $(k+2)$-complete.
nodes.section: 6 Decomposition into paths of even length

nodes.name: Bad vertex
nodes.statement:
Suppose, for a contradiction, that \(\mathcal{B}\) is not \((k+2)\)-complete.
	Then there is a vertex \(v\) of \(G\) such that \(\mathrm{hang}(v,\mathcal{B}) \leq k+2\).
	Suppose, without loss of generality, that \(v\) is a vertex of \(A\).
	Since \(\mathcal{B}\) is \((2k+3)\)-pre-complete, \(\mathrm{preHang}(v,\mathcal{B}) \geq 2k+4\).
	Thus, there are at least \(k+2\) pre-hanging edges at \(v\) 
	that are not hanging edges at \(v\), say \(x_1v,\ldots,x_{k+2}v\).
	Let \(T_1 = y_0y_1\cdots y_{2k+2}\) be the element of \(\mathcal{B}\) that contains \(x_1v\),
	where, without loss of generality, \(y_0 = x_1\) and \(y_1 = v\).
	The vertices of \(T_1\) in \(B\) are \(y_0,y_2,\ldots, y_{2k+2}\).
	First, we will show that for some $x_i\notin V(T_1)$ for some \(2\leq i \leq k+2\).
nodes.statement_short: Take $v\in A$ with few hanging edges; pre-completeness gives many non-hanging pre-hanging edges $x_iv$.
nodes.section: 6 Decomposition into paths of even length

nodes.name: Find x_i outside T_1
nodes.statement:
Since \(y_2\) is in \(B\) and \(y_0\) is the end-vertex of \(T_1\) in \(B\), 
	the vertex \(y_2\) is not an end-vertex of \(T_1\). 
	Since \(y_1y_2 \in E(T_1)\), the edge \(y_1y_2\) is not a pre-hanging edge at \(v\).
	Then, \(y_2 \neq x_i\) for every \(2\leq i\leq k+2\). 
	Therefore, \(|\{y_4, y_6,\ldots,y_{2k+2}\}| = k\) and \(|\{2,\ldots,k+2\}| = k+1\), 
	from where we conclude that for at least one \(i\), we have \(x_i \notin V(T_1)\).
nodes.statement_short: Counting the $B$-vertices of $T_1$ shows some $x_i\notin V(T_1)$.
nodes.section: 6 Decomposition into paths of even length

nodes.name: Swap edges
nodes.statement:
Now let \(T_i = z_0z_1\cdots z_{2k+2}\) be the element of \(\mathcal{B}\) that contains \(x_iv\).
	Suppose, without loss of generality, that \(z_1 = v\) and \(z_0 = x_i\).
	Let \(T'_1 = vy_1\cdots y_{2k+1}\) and \(T'_i = y_0 z_1\cdots z_{2k+2}\)
	and let \(\mathcal{B}' = \mathcal{B} - T_1 - T_i + T'_1 + T'_i\).
	We note that \(\bar T'_1 = \bar T_1 - x_1v + x_iv\) and \(\bar T'_i = \bar T_i -x_iv + x_1v\).
	Since \(x_i \notin V(T_1)\), we have \(d_{T'_1}(x_i) = 1\), which 
implies that \(x_iv\) is a hanging edge of \(\mathcal{B}'\) at \(v\).
	Therefore, \(\sum_{v\in V(G)} \mathrm{hang}(v,\mathcal{B}') > 
			\sum_{v\in V(G)} \mathrm{hang}(v,\mathcal{B})\).
nodes.statement_short: Exchange $x_1v$ and $x_iv$ between $T_1$ and $T_i$, creating a new hanging edge.

nodes.name: Balance preserved; contradiction
nodes.statement:
We claim that \(\mathcal{B}'\) is \(\mathbb{F}\)-balanced.
	Indeed, since the set of pre-hanging edges at~\(v\) is the same in 
\(\mathcal{B}\) and \(\mathcal{B}'\),
	we have \(\mathcal{B}(v) = \mathcal{B}'(v)\) for every \(v\) in \(V(G)\).
	Therefore, \(\mathcal{B}'\) is an \(\mathbb{F}\)-balanced 
\((2k+3)\)-pre-complete
	decomposition such that 
	\(\sum_{v\in V(G)} \mathrm{hang}(v,\mathcal{B}') > 
			\sum_{v\in V(G)} \mathrm{hang}(v,\mathcal{B})\),
	a contradiction to the choice of \(\mathcal{B}\).
nodes.statement_short: Pre-hanging edges are unchanged, so $\mathcal{B}'$ is balanced, contradicting maximality.

nodes.name: End-counts unchanged
nodes.statement:
Indeed, since the set of pre-hanging edges at~\(v\) is the same in 
\(\mathcal{B}\) and \(\mathcal{B}'\),
	we have \(\mathcal{B}(v) = \mathcal{B}'(v)\) for every \(v\) in \(V(G)\).
nodes.statement_short: Pre-hanging edges are the same, so $\mathcal{B}'(v)=\mathcal{B}(v)$.
nodes.section: 6 Decomposition into paths of even length

nodes.name: Contradiction
nodes.statement:
Therefore, \(\mathcal{B}'\) is an \(\mathbb{F}\)-balanced 
\((2k+3)\)-pre-complete
	decomposition such that 
	\(\sum_{v\in V(G)} \mathrm{hang}(v,\mathcal{B}') > 
			\sum_{v\in V(G)} \mathrm{hang}(v,\mathcal{B})\),
	a contradiction to the choice of \(\mathcal{B}\).
nodes.statement_short: $\mathcal{B}'$ has more hanging edges, contradicting the choice of $\mathcal{B}$.

nodes.name: Balanced complete path decomposition via disentangling (even case)
nodes.statement:
Let \(k\) be a positive integer and let \(G\) be a bipartitte graph that admits a 
	\(\big(2,2(2k+2)\big)\)-bifactorization \(\mathbb{F}\).
	If \(G\) admits an \(\mathbb{F}\)-balanced \((k+2)\)-complete 
	vanilla $(2k+2)$-tracking decomposition, 
	then \(G\) admits an \(\mathbb{F}\)-balanced \((k+2)\)-complete 
	$(2k+2)$-path tracking decomposition.
assumptions:
Let \(k\) be a positive integer and let \(G\) be a bipartitte graph that admits a 
	\(\big(2,2(2k+2)\big)\)-bifactorization \(\mathbb{F}\)

nodes.label: lemma:even-path-dec

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 6.4
nodes.statement:
Let \(k\) be a positive integer and let \(G = (A,B;E)\) be a 
	bipartite graph that admits a 
	\(\big(2,2(2k+2)\big)\)-bifactorization \(\mathbb{F}\).
	Suppose $G$ admits an \(\mathbb{F}\)-balanced 
	\((k+2)\)-complete
	$(2k+2)$-tracking decomposition $\mathcal{B}$.
	By Lemma~\ref{lemma:disentangling} (applied with \(\ell = 2k+2\)),
	the graph \(G\) admits a \((k+2)\)-complete tracking decomposition \(\mathcal{B}'\)
	such that \(\mathcal{B}'(v) = \mathcal{B}(v)\)
	for every vertex \(v\) of \(G\).
	Therefore, \(\mathcal{B}'\) is an \(\mathbb{F}\)-balanced 
	$(k+2)$-complete $(2k+2)$-tracking decomposition.
nodes.statement_short: Apply the Disentangling Lemma with $\ell=2k+2$; end-counts, hence balance, are preserved.

nodes.name: Balanced even path decomposition from a strong bifactorization
nodes.statement:
Let \(k\) be a positive integer. 
	If \(G\) is a bipartite graph that 
admits a strong 
	\(\big(2,2(2k+2)\big)\)-bifactorization \(\mathbb{F}\),
	then \(G\) admits an \(\mathbb{F}\)-balanced $(2k+2)$-path 
tracking decomposition.
assumptions:
\(G\) is a bipartite graph that 
admits a strong 
	\(\big(2,2(2k+2)\big)\)-bifactorization \(\mathbb{F}\)
nodes.section: 6 Decomposition into paths of even length
nodes.label: thm:even-path-decomposition

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 6.5
nodes.statement:
The proof is by induction on \(k\).
By Lemma~\ref{lemma:2-PD}, the statement is true for \(k = 0\).
Thus, suppose \(k>0\),
and let \(G = (A_1,A_2;E)\) be a bipartite graph that admits a strong 
\(\big(2,2(2k+2)\big)\)-bifactorization 
\(\mathbb{F} = (\mathcal{F}_1,\mathcal{F}_2)\).
We claim that \(G\) admits an \(\mathbb{F}\)-balanced 
\((2k+3)\)-pre-complete
vanilla $(2k+2)$-trail decomposition. Let \(\mathcal{F}_1 = 
\{M_1,N_1,F_{1,1},\ldots,F_{1,2k+1}\}\) 
and \(\mathcal{F}_2 = \{M_2,N_2,F_{2,1},\ldots,F_{2,2k+1}\}\), and let \(G_i = 
G\big[\bigcup_{F\in\mathcal{F}_i} F\big]\) for \(i = 1,2\). 
Hereafter, fix \(i\in\{1,2\}\).

Define \(d^*(v) = d_{G_i}(v)/\big(2(2k+2)\big)\) for every vertex $v\in A_i$.
Note that \(d_{F_{i,j}}(v) = 2d^*(v) = 2d_{M_i}(v) = 2d_{N_i}(v)\) for every 
vertex \(v\) in \(A_i\)
and \(1\leq j\leq 2k+1\).
For \(j \in \{2k,2k+1\}\), let \(O_{F_{i,j}}\) be an Eulerian 
orientation of \(G[F_{i,j}]\).
Let \(F_{i,j} = F_{i,j}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits} \cup F_{i,j}^{\mathop{\text{\rm back}}\nolimits}\), where 
\(F_{i,j}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}\) is the set of edges
of \(F_{i,j}\) leaving $A_i$ in \(O_{F_{i,j}}\), and 
\(F_{i,j}^{\mathop{\text{\rm back}}\nolimits}\) 
is the set of edges
of \(F_{i,j}\) entering $A_i$ in~\(O_{F_{i,j}}\).


Let \(G' = G - M_1 - N_1 - M_2 - N_2 - F_{1,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits} - F_{1,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits} 
	- F_{2,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits} - F_{2,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}\),
and let \(\mathcal{F}'_i = 
\{F_{i,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm back}}\nolimits},F_{i,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm back}}\nolimits},F_{i,1},\ldots, 
F_{i,2k-1}\}\).
Let \(G'_i = G\big[\bigcup_{F\in\mathcal{F}'_i} F\big]\).
Note that \(G'_i = G_i - M_i - N_i - F_{i,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits} - F_{i,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}\).
Then, for every $v\in A_i$, we have
\begin{equation} d_{G'_i}(v) = d_{G_i}(v) - 4d^*(v)
	    = 2(2k+2)d^*(v) - 4d^*(v)
	    = 2(2k)d^*(v).
\end{equation}

\begin{claim}
\(\mathbb{F}' = (\mathcal{F}'_1,\mathcal{F}'_2)\) 
is a strong \(\big(2,2(2k)\big)\)-bifactorization of \(G'\).
\end{claim}

\begin{proof}
To prove this claim, we shall prove the following.
\begin{itemize}
	\item[(i)] \(F_{i,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm back}}\nolimits}\) and \(F_{i,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm back}}\nolimits}\) 
			are \(\big(A_i,1,2(2k)\big)\)-factors of \(G'_i\);
	\item[(ii)] \(F_{i,j}\) is an Eulerian \(\big(A_i,2,2(2k)\big)\)-factor 
			of \(G'_i\) for \(j = 1,\ldots,2k-1\);
	\item[(iii)] \(d_{G'_i}(v) \geq (2k)(2k+2)\) for every vertex \(v\in 
A_i\).\\
\end{itemize}

To prove items (i) and (ii), first note that, for every $v\in A_i$, we have
 \(d_{F_{i,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm back}}\nolimits}}(v) = d_{F_{i,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm back}}\nolimits}}(v) = d^*(v)\) 
and \(d_{F_{i,j}}(v) = 2d^*(v)\) for every \(1\leq j\leq 2k-1\). 
By~\eqref{even-d}, we conclude that \(F_{i,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm back}}\nolimits}\) and 
\(F_{i,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm back}}\nolimits}\) are \(\big(A_i,1,2(2k)\big)\)-factors of \(G'_i\), and 
\(F_{i,j}\) is an \(\big(A_i,2,2(2k)\big)\)-factor of \(G'_i\).
Since \(\mathbb{F}\) is a \(\big(2,2(2k+2)\big)\)-bifactorization,
\(F_{1,j}\) and \(F_{2,j}\) are Eulerian graphs for 
\(1\leq j\leq 2k-1\).

It remains to prove item (iii). 
Since \(d_{G'_i}(v) = 2(2k)d^*(v)\) and \(d^*(v) = d_{G_i}(v)/\big(2(2k+2)\big)\) 
for every vertex \(v\in A_i\),
we have \(d_{G'_i}(v) = \frac{2(2k)}{2(2k+2)}d_{G_1}(v)\) for every \(v\in 
A_i\).
Since \(\mathbb{F}\) is a strong \(\big(2,2(2k+2)\big)\)-bifactorization, 
we have \(d_{G_i}(v) \geq (2k+2)(2k+4)\) for every \(v\in A_i\).
Thus \(d_{G'_i}(v) \geq (2k)(2k+4) > (2k)(2k+2)\) for every \(v\in A_i\).
\end{proof}

Since \(\mathbb{F}'\) is a strong \(\big(2,2(2k)\big)\)-bifactorization of \(G'\),
by the induction hypothesis, \(G'\) admits an \(\mathbb{F}'\)-balanced 
$2k$-path tracking decomposition \(\mathcal{B}'\).

Since \(\mathcal{B}'\) is an \(\mathbb{F}'\)-balanced $2k$-path tracking decomposition, we have 
	\begin{itemize}
		\item \(\mathcal{B}'(v) = d_{G'_1}(v)/2k
			+ d_{F_{2,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm back}}\nolimits}}(v)
			+ d_{F_{2,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm back}}\nolimits}}(v)\) for every \(v\in A_1\);
		\item \(\mathcal{B}'(v) = d_{G'_2}(v)/2k
			+ d_{F_{1,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm back}}\nolimits}}(v)
			+ d_{F_{1,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm back}}\nolimits}}(v)\) for every \(v\in A_2\).
	\end{itemize}


Now we want to extend each $2k$-path of \(\mathcal{B}'\) to obtain a \((2k+2)\)-tracking decomposition of $G$. 

For that, we add edges from 
\(E(G)-E(G')\) at the end-vertices of the trackings in $\mathcal{B}'$.
For each vertex \(v\in A_1\) ($v\in A_2$), let \(S_v\) be the set of edges 
of \(M_1\cup N_1 \cup F_{2,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}\cup F_{2,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}\) (\(M_2\cup N_2 
\cup F_{1,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}\cup F_{1,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}\)) incident to \(v\).
Note that for each edge \(e\) in \(E(G)-E(G')\) there is exactly 
one \(v\in V(G)\) such that \(e\in S_v\).
Then, \(\bigcup_{v\in V(G)} S_v=E(G) - E(G')\). Therefore, if we prove that 
\(\mathcal{B}'(v) = |S_v|\), then we can extend every tracking $B$ of $\mathcal{B}'$ by adding 
one edge at each end-vertex of $B$.

\begin{claim}
	 \(\mathcal{B}'(v) = |S_v|\), for every $v\in V(G)$.
\end{claim}

\begin{proof}
First, note that, since \(F_{2,2k}\) and \(F_{2,2k+1}\) are Eulerian, 
we have \(d_{F_{2,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm back}}\nolimits}}(v) = d_{F_{2,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(v)\) 
and \(d_{F_{2,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm back}}\nolimits}}(v) = d_{F_{2,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(v)\)
for every vertex \(v\) in \(A_1\),
and since \(F_{1,2k}\) and \(F_{1,2k+1}\) are Eulerian, we have 
\(d_{F_{1,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm back}}\nolimits}}(v) = d_{F_{1,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(v)\) and 
\(d_{F_{1,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm back}}\nolimits}}(v) = d_{F_{1,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(v)\)
for every vertex \(v\) in \(A_2\).

For every \(v\in A_i\) and every \(1\leq j\leq 2k-1\), 
we have \(d_{G'_i}(v)/(2(2k)) = d_{F_{i,j}}(v)/2 = d^*(v)\).
Now, recall that for each vertex \(v\in A_i\), we have \(d_{M_i}(v) = 
d_{N_i}(v) = d^*(v)\).
Therefore, for every $v\in A_1$, we have 
\begin{align*}
	 \mathcal{B}'(v) & = d_{G'_1}(v)/(2k) + d_{F_{2,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm back}}\nolimits}}(v) + 
d_{F_{2,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm back}}\nolimits}}(v) \\
			& = 2d^*(v) + d_{F_{2,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(v) + 
d_{F_{2,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(v)\\
			& = d_{M_1}(v) + d_{N_1}(v) + d_{F_{2,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(v) + 
d_{F_{2,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(v)\\
			& = |S_v|.
\end{align*}
Similarly, we have $\mathcal{B}'(v)=|S_v|$ for every $v\in A_2$.
\end{proof}

We have shown that every tracking \(B\) of 
\(\mathcal{B}'\) can be extended by adding one edge at each of its end-vertices.
Let \(\mathcal{B}\) be the decomposition obtained with these extensions.




Analogously to the odd case, we conclude that \(\mathcal{B}\) is a \((2k+2)\)-tracking decomposition of~\(G\).

\begin{claim}
\(\mathcal{B}\) is \(\mathbb{F}\)-balanced.
\end{claim}

\begin{proof}

Let \(x_0\) be a vertex in \(A\). First we will prove that \(\mathcal{B}(x_0) \leq 
d_{F_{1,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(x_0) + d_{F_{1,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(x_0) 
+ d_{M_2}(x_0) + d_{N_2}(x_0)\).
If there is no tracking \(T = x_0x_1\cdots x_{2k+2}\) in $\mathcal{B}$, where $x_0x_1$ is an 
edge of \(E(G)-E(G')\), then $\mathcal{B}(x_0)=0$. 
For every such tracking $T$, by the 
construction of $\mathcal{B}$, we know that $x_0x_1$ is an element of $S_{x_1}$.
Since \(x_1\) is a vertex of \(A_2\), we have 
that \(S_{x_1} \subset M_2\cup N_2 \cup F_{1,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits} \cup 
F_{1,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}\).
Therefore,
\begin{equation*}
\mathcal{B}(x_0) \leq d_{F_{1,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(x_0) + d_{F_{1,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(x_0) 
+ d_{M_2}(x_0) + d_{N_2}(x_0).
\end{equation*}
Now we will prove that $\mathcal{B}(x_0)\geq d_{F_{1,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(x_0) + 
d_{F_{1,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(x_0) + d_{M_2}(x_0) + d_{N_2}(x_0)$.
Note that if \(x_0x_1\) is an edge of 
\(M_2\cup N_2 \cup F_{1,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits} \cup F_{1,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}\)
that is incident to \(x_0\) in $A_1$ \big(these are the only edges of $G$ that 
can contribute to $\mathcal{B}(x_0)$\big), then, by the construction of $\mathcal{B}$, there is a 
tracking \(Q' = x_1\cdots x_{2k+2}\) of a path such that the tracking  \(Q = x_0x_1\cdots 
x_{2k+2}\)\(x_0\) (of a vanilla trail) belongs to $\mathcal{B}$.
Therefore, \(\mathcal{B}(x_0) = d_{F_{1,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(x_0) + d_{F_{1,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(x_0) 
				+ d_{M_2}(x_0) + d_{N_2}(x_0)\).
Thus, for every vertex \(v\in A_1\) we have 
\begin{align*}
	\mathcal{B}(v)	&= |F_{1,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}(v)| + |F_{1,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}(v)| + |M_2(v)| + 
|N_2(v)| \\
			&= 2d^*(v) + d_{M_2}(v) + d_{N_2}(v) \\
			&= d_{G_1}(v)/(2k+2) + d_{M_2}(v) + d_{N_2}(v).
\end{align*}
Analogously, we have \(\mathcal{B}(v) = d_{G_2}(v)/(2k+2) + d_{M_1}(v) + d_{N_1}(v)\)
for each vertex \(v\in A_2\).
Thus, \(\mathcal{B}\) is an \(\mathbb{F}\)-balanced vanilla $(2k+2)$-trail decomposition.
\end{proof}

\begin{claim}
\(\mathcal{B}\) is \((2k+3)\)-pre-complete.
\end{claim}

\begin{proof}
Let  \(v\in A_i\).
We shall prove that \(\mathrm{preHang}(v,\mathcal{B}) > 2k+3\).
Note that, by the construction of $\mathcal{B}$, the set of pre-hanging edges at \(v\) 
in \(\mathcal{B}\)
is exactly \(S_v\).
Then, \(\mathrm{preHang}(v,\mathcal{B}) = |S_v| = \mathcal{B}'(v)\).
Since \(\mathcal{B}'\) is balanced, \(\mathcal{B}'(v) \geq d_{G'_i}(v)/(2k)\).
Therefore,
\begin{equation*}
	\mathrm{preHang}(v,\mathcal{B})	= \mathcal{B}'(v) 
					\geq d_{G'_i}(v)/(2k) 
					= 2d^*(v) 
					= d_{G_i}(v)/(2k+2).
\end{equation*} 
Since \(\mathbb{F}\) is a strong \(\big(2,2(2k+2)\big)\)-bifactorization of \(G\),
we have \(d_{G_i}(v) \geq (2k+2)(2k+4)\), from where we conclude that  
\(\mathrm{preHang}(v,\mathcal{B}) \geq 2k+4\).
Therefore, \(\mathcal{B}\) is a \((2k+3)\)-pre-complete vanilla trail decomposition.
\end{proof}







Now, analogously to the odd case, using Lemmas~\ref{lemma:even-complete} and~\ref{lemma:even-path-dec}, we conclude that \(G\) admits an \(\mathbb{F}\)-balanced $(2k+2)$-path tracking decomposition.
nodes.statement_short: Induction on $k$ from Lemma 6.2. Remove two matchings and halves of two oriented Eulerian factors, decompose by induction, extend each path by one edge at each end, then apply Lemmas 6.3 and 6.4.

nodes.name: Base case
nodes.statement:
The proof is by induction on \(k\).
By Lemma~\ref{lemma:2-PD}, the statement is true for \(k = 0\).
nodes.statement_short: Induction on $k$; $k=0$ is Lemma 6.2.
nodes.section: 6 Decomposition into paths of even length

nodes.name: Inductive setup
nodes.statement:
Thus, suppose \(k>0\),
and let \(G = (A_1,A_2;E)\) be a bipartite graph that admits a strong 
\(\big(2,2(2k+2)\big)\)-bifactorization 
\(\mathbb{F} = (\mathcal{F}_1,\mathcal{F}_2)\).
We claim that \(G\) admits an \(\mathbb{F}\)-balanced 
\((2k+3)\)-pre-complete
vanilla $(2k+2)$-trail decomposition. Let \(\mathcal{F}_1 = 
\{M_1,N_1,F_{1,1},\ldots,F_{1,2k+1}\}\) 
and \(\mathcal{F}_2 = \{M_2,N_2,F_{2,1},\ldots,F_{2,2k+1}\}\), and let \(G_i = 
G\big[\bigcup_{F\in\mathcal{F}_i} F\big]\) for \(i = 1,2\). 
Hereafter, fix \(i\in\{1,2\}\).
nodes.statement_short: Take a strong $(2,2(2k+2))$-bifactorization; aim for a balanced pre-complete trail decomposition.
nodes.section: 6 Decomposition into paths of even length

nodes.name: Orient two 2-factors
nodes.statement:
Define \(d^*(v) = d_{G_i}(v)/\big(2(2k+2)\big)\) for every vertex $v\in A_i$.
Note that \(d_{F_{i,j}}(v) = 2d^*(v) = 2d_{M_i}(v) = 2d_{N_i}(v)\) for every 
vertex \(v\) in \(A_i\)
and \(1\leq j\leq 2k+1\).
For \(j \in \{2k,2k+1\}\), let \(O_{F_{i,j}}\) be an Eulerian 
orientation of \(G[F_{i,j}]\).
Let \(F_{i,j} = F_{i,j}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits} \cup F_{i,j}^{\mathop{\text{\rm back}}\nolimits}\), where 
\(F_{i,j}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}\) is the set of edges
of \(F_{i,j}\) leaving $A_i$ in \(O_{F_{i,j}}\), and 
\(F_{i,j}^{\mathop{\text{\rm back}}\nolimits}\) 
is the set of edges
of \(F_{i,j}\) entering $A_i$ in~\(O_{F_{i,j}}\).
nodes.statement_short: Split $F_{i,2k}$, $F_{i,2k+1}$ via Eulerian orientations.
nodes.section: 6 Decomposition into paths of even length

nodes.name: Reduced graph G'
nodes.statement:
Let \(G' = G - M_1 - N_1 - M_2 - N_2 - F_{1,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits} - F_{1,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits} 
	- F_{2,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits} - F_{2,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}\),
and let \(\mathcal{F}'_i = 
\{F_{i,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm back}}\nolimits},F_{i,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm back}}\nolimits},F_{i,1},\ldots, 
F_{i,2k-1}\}\).
Let \(G'_i = G\big[\bigcup_{F\in\mathcal{F}'_i} F\big]\).
Note that \(G'_i = G_i - M_i - N_i - F_{i,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits} - F_{i,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}\).
Then, for every $v\in A_i$, we have
\begin{equation} d_{G'_i}(v) = d_{G_i}(v) - 4d^*(v)
	    = 2(2k+2)d^*(v) - 4d^*(v)
	    = 2(2k)d^*(v).
\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Remove matchings and forward halves; degrees on $A_i$ become $2(2k)d^*(v)$.
nodes.section: 6 Decomposition into paths of even length

nodes.name: Claim 6.6
nodes.statement:
\begin{claim}
\(\mathbb{F}' = (\mathcal{F}'_1,\mathcal{F}'_2)\) 
is a strong \(\big(2,2(2k)\big)\)-bifactorization of \(G'\).
\end{claim}

\begin{proof}
To prove this claim, we shall prove the following.
\begin{itemize}
	\item[(i)] \(F_{i,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm back}}\nolimits}\) and \(F_{i,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm back}}\nolimits}\) 
			are \(\big(A_i,1,2(2k)\big)\)-factors of \(G'_i\);
	\item[(ii)] \(F_{i,j}\) is an Eulerian \(\big(A_i,2,2(2k)\big)\)-factor 
			of \(G'_i\) for \(j = 1,\ldots,2k-1\);
	\item[(iii)] \(d_{G'_i}(v) \geq (2k)(2k+2)\) for every vertex \(v\in 
A_i\).\\
\end{itemize}

To prove items (i) and (ii), first note that, for every $v\in A_i$, we have
 \(d_{F_{i,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm back}}\nolimits}}(v) = d_{F_{i,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm back}}\nolimits}}(v) = d^*(v)\) 
and \(d_{F_{i,j}}(v) = 2d^*(v)\) for every \(1\leq j\leq 2k-1\). 
By~\eqref{even-d}, we conclude that \(F_{i,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm back}}\nolimits}\) and 
\(F_{i,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm back}}\nolimits}\) are \(\big(A_i,1,2(2k)\big)\)-factors of \(G'_i\), and 
\(F_{i,j}\) is an \(\big(A_i,2,2(2k)\big)\)-factor of \(G'_i\).
Since \(\mathbb{F}\) is a \(\big(2,2(2k+2)\big)\)-bifactorization,
\(F_{1,j}\) and \(F_{2,j}\) are Eulerian graphs for 
\(1\leq j\leq 2k-1\).

It remains to prove item (iii). 
Since \(d_{G'_i}(v) = 2(2k)d^*(v)\) and \(d^*(v) = d_{G_i}(v)/\big(2(2k+2)\big)\) 
for every vertex \(v\in A_i\),
we have \(d_{G'_i}(v) = \frac{2(2k)}{2(2k+2)}d_{G_1}(v)\) for every \(v\in 
A_i\).
Since \(\mathbb{F}\) is a strong \(\big(2,2(2k+2)\big)\)-bifactorization, 
we have \(d_{G_i}(v) \geq (2k+2)(2k+4)\) for every \(v\in A_i\).
Thus \(d_{G'_i}(v) \geq (2k)(2k+4) > (2k)(2k+2)\) for every \(v\in A_i\).
\end{proof}

nodes.section: 6 Decomposition into paths of even length

nodes.name: Apply induction
nodes.statement:
Since \(\mathbb{F}'\) is a strong \(\big(2,2(2k)\big)\)-bifactorization of \(G'\),
by the induction hypothesis, \(G'\) admits an \(\mathbb{F}'\)-balanced 
$2k$-path tracking decomposition \(\mathcal{B}'\).
nodes.statement_short: Induction gives a balanced $2k$-path decomposition of $G'$.
nodes.section: 6 Decomposition into paths of even length

nodes.name: End-counts of B'
nodes.statement:
Since \(\mathcal{B}'\) is an \(\mathbb{F}'\)-balanced $2k$-path tracking decomposition, we have 
	\begin{itemize}
		\item \(\mathcal{B}'(v) = d_{G'_1}(v)/2k
			+ d_{F_{2,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm back}}\nolimits}}(v)
			+ d_{F_{2,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm back}}\nolimits}}(v)\) for every \(v\in A_1\);
		\item \(\mathcal{B}'(v) = d_{G'_2}(v)/2k
			+ d_{F_{1,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm back}}\nolimits}}(v)
			+ d_{F_{1,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm back}}\nolimits}}(v)\) for every \(v\in A_2\).
nodes.statement_short: Write out the end-counts of $\mathcal{B}'$.
nodes.section: 6 Decomposition into paths of even length

nodes.name: Edge sets S_v
nodes.statement:
Now we want to extend each $2k$-path of \(\mathcal{B}'\) to obtain a \((2k+2)\)-tracking decomposition of $G$. 

For that, we add edges from 
\(E(G)-E(G')\) at the end-vertices of the trackings in $\mathcal{B}'$.
For each vertex \(v\in A_1\) ($v\in A_2$), let \(S_v\) be the set of edges 
of \(M_1\cup N_1 \cup F_{2,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}\cup F_{2,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}\) (\(M_2\cup N_2 
\cup F_{1,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}\cup F_{1,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}\)) incident to \(v\).
Note that for each edge \(e\) in \(E(G)-E(G')\) there is exactly 
one \(v\in V(G)\) such that \(e\in S_v\).
Then, \(\bigcup_{v\in V(G)} S_v=E(G) - E(G')\). Therefore, if we prove that 
\(\mathcal{B}'(v) = |S_v|\), then we can extend every tracking $B$ of $\mathcal{B}'$ by adding 
one edge at each end-vertex of $B$.
nodes.statement_short: Assign removed edges to vertices as $S_v$; need $\mathcal{B}'(v)=|S_v|$.
nodes.section: 6 Decomposition into paths of even length

nodes.name: Claim 6.7
nodes.statement:
\begin{claim}
	 \(\mathcal{B}'(v) = |S_v|\), for every $v\in V(G)$.
\end{claim}

\begin{proof}
First, note that, since \(F_{2,2k}\) and \(F_{2,2k+1}\) are Eulerian, 
we have \(d_{F_{2,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm back}}\nolimits}}(v) = d_{F_{2,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(v)\) 
and \(d_{F_{2,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm back}}\nolimits}}(v) = d_{F_{2,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(v)\)
for every vertex \(v\) in \(A_1\),
and since \(F_{1,2k}\) and \(F_{1,2k+1}\) are Eulerian, we have 
\(d_{F_{1,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm back}}\nolimits}}(v) = d_{F_{1,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(v)\) and 
\(d_{F_{1,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm back}}\nolimits}}(v) = d_{F_{1,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(v)\)
for every vertex \(v\) in \(A_2\).

For every \(v\in A_i\) and every \(1\leq j\leq 2k-1\), 
we have \(d_{G'_i}(v)/(2(2k)) = d_{F_{i,j}}(v)/2 = d^*(v)\).
Now, recall that for each vertex \(v\in A_i\), we have \(d_{M_i}(v) = 
d_{N_i}(v) = d^*(v)\).
Therefore, for every $v\in A_1$, we have 
\begin{align*}
	 \mathcal{B}'(v) & = d_{G'_1}(v)/(2k) + d_{F_{2,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm back}}\nolimits}}(v) + 
d_{F_{2,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm back}}\nolimits}}(v) \\
			& = 2d^*(v) + d_{F_{2,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(v) + 
d_{F_{2,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(v)\\
			& = d_{M_1}(v) + d_{N_1}(v) + d_{F_{2,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(v) + 
d_{F_{2,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(v)\\
			& = |S_v|.
\end{align*}
Similarly, we have $\mathcal{B}'(v)=|S_v|$ for every $v\in A_2$.
\end{proof}
nodes.statement_short: Claim 6.7 and its proof.
nodes.section: 6 Decomposition into paths of even length

nodes.name: Extend paths
nodes.statement:
We have shown that every tracking \(B\) of 
\(\mathcal{B}'\) can be extended by adding one edge at each of its end-vertices.
Let \(\mathcal{B}\) be the decomposition obtained with these extensions.




Analogously to the odd case, we conclude that \(\mathcal{B}\) is a \((2k+2)\)-tracking decomposition of~\(G\).
nodes.statement_short: Extend each path at both ends to get a $(2k+2)$-tracking decomposition.

nodes.name: Claim 6.8
nodes.statement:
\begin{claim}
\(\mathcal{B}\) is \(\mathbb{F}\)-balanced.
\end{claim}

\begin{proof}

Let \(x_0\) be a vertex in \(A\). First we will prove that \(\mathcal{B}(x_0) \leq 
d_{F_{1,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(x_0) + d_{F_{1,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(x_0) 
+ d_{M_2}(x_0) + d_{N_2}(x_0)\).
If there is no tracking \(T = x_0x_1\cdots x_{2k+2}\) in $\mathcal{B}$, where $x_0x_1$ is an 
edge of \(E(G)-E(G')\), then $\mathcal{B}(x_0)=0$. 
For every such tracking $T$, by the 
construction of $\mathcal{B}$, we know that $x_0x_1$ is an element of $S_{x_1}$.
Since \(x_1\) is a vertex of \(A_2\), we have 
that \(S_{x_1} \subset M_2\cup N_2 \cup F_{1,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits} \cup 
F_{1,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}\).
Therefore,
\begin{equation*}
\mathcal{B}(x_0) \leq d_{F_{1,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(x_0) + d_{F_{1,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(x_0) 
+ d_{M_2}(x_0) + d_{N_2}(x_0).
\end{equation*}
Now we will prove that $\mathcal{B}(x_0)\geq d_{F_{1,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(x_0) + 
d_{F_{1,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(x_0) + d_{M_2}(x_0) + d_{N_2}(x_0)$.
Note that if \(x_0x_1\) is an edge of 
\(M_2\cup N_2 \cup F_{1,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits} \cup F_{1,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}\)
that is incident to \(x_0\) in $A_1$ \big(these are the only edges of $G$ that 
can contribute to $\mathcal{B}(x_0)$\big), then, by the construction of $\mathcal{B}$, there is a 
tracking \(Q' = x_1\cdots x_{2k+2}\) of a path such that the tracking  \(Q = x_0x_1\cdots 
x_{2k+2}\)\(x_0\) (of a vanilla trail) belongs to $\mathcal{B}$.
Therefore, \(\mathcal{B}(x_0) = d_{F_{1,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(x_0) + d_{F_{1,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(x_0) 
				+ d_{M_2}(x_0) + d_{N_2}(x_0)\).
Thus, for every vertex \(v\in A_1\) we have 
\begin{align*}
	\mathcal{B}(v)	&= |F_{1,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}(v)| + |F_{1,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}(v)| + |M_2(v)| + 
|N_2(v)| \\
			&= 2d^*(v) + d_{M_2}(v) + d_{N_2}(v) \\
			&= d_{G_1}(v)/(2k+2) + d_{M_2}(v) + d_{N_2}(v).
\end{align*}
Analogously, we have \(\mathcal{B}(v) = d_{G_2}(v)/(2k+2) + d_{M_1}(v) + d_{N_1}(v)\)
for each vertex \(v\in A_2\).
Thus, \(\mathcal{B}\) is an \(\mathbb{F}\)-balanced vanilla $(2k+2)$-trail decomposition.
\end{proof}

nodes.name: Claim 6.9
nodes.statement:
\begin{claim}
\(\mathcal{B}\) is \((2k+3)\)-pre-complete.
\end{claim}

\begin{proof}
Let  \(v\in A_i\).
We shall prove that \(\mathrm{preHang}(v,\mathcal{B}) > 2k+3\).
Note that, by the construction of $\mathcal{B}$, the set of pre-hanging edges at \(v\) 
in \(\mathcal{B}\)
is exactly \(S_v\).
Then, \(\mathrm{preHang}(v,\mathcal{B}) = |S_v| = \mathcal{B}'(v)\).
Since \(\mathcal{B}'\) is balanced, \(\mathcal{B}'(v) \geq d_{G'_i}(v)/(2k)\).
Therefore,
\begin{equation*}
	\mathrm{preHang}(v,\mathcal{B})	= \mathcal{B}'(v) 
					\geq d_{G'_i}(v)/(2k) 
					= 2d^*(v) 
					= d_{G_i}(v)/(2k+2).
\end{equation*} 
Since \(\mathbb{F}\) is a strong \(\big(2,2(2k+2)\big)\)-bifactorization of \(G\),
we have \(d_{G_i}(v) \geq (2k+2)(2k+4)\), from where we conclude that  
\(\mathrm{preHang}(v,\mathcal{B}) \geq 2k+4\).
Therefore, \(\mathcal{B}\) is a \((2k+3)\)-pre-complete vanilla trail decomposition.
\end{proof}
nodes.statement_short: Claim 6.9 and its proof.

d_{F_{1,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(x_0) + d_{M_2}(x_0) + d_{N_2}(x_0)$.
Note that if \(x_0x_1\) is an edge of 
\(M_2\cup N_2 \cup F_{1,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits} \cup F_{1,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}\)
that is incident to \(x_0\) in $A_1$ \big(these are the only edges of $G$ that 
can contribute to $\mathcal{B}(x_0)$\big), then, by the construction of $\mathcal{B}$, there is a 
tracking \(Q' = x_1\cdots x_{2k+2}\) of a path such that the tracking  \(Q = x_0x_1\cdots 
x_{2k+2}\)\(x_0\) (of a vanilla trail) belongs to $\mathcal{B}$.
Therefore, \(\mathcal{B}(x_0) = d_{F_{1,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(x_0) + d_{F_{1,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(x_0) 
				+ d_{M_2}(x_0) + d_{N_2}(x_0)\).
Thus, for every vertex \(v\in A_1\) we have 
\begin{align*}
	\mathcal{B}(v)	&= |F_{1,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}(v)| + |F_{1,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}(v)| + |M_2(v)| + 
|N_2(v)| \\
			&= 2d^*(v) + d_{M_2}(v) + d_{N_2}(v) \\
			&= d_{G_1}(v)/(2k+2) + d_{M_2}(v) + d_{N_2}(v).
\end{align*}
Analogously, we have \(\mathcal{B}(v) = d_{G_2}(v)/(2k+2) + d_{M_1}(v) + d_{N_1}(v)\)
for each vertex \(v\in A_2\).
Thus, \(\mathcal{B}\) is an \(\mathbb{F}\)-balanced vanilla $(2k+2)$-trail decomposition.
nodes.statement_short: Two-sided count: end-edges at $x_0$ come exactly from the $S_{x_1}$ sets, giving equality with the balance formula.

nodes.name: Upper bound
nodes.statement:
Let \(x_0\) be a vertex in \(A\). First we will prove that \(\mathcal{B}(x_0) \leq 
d_{F_{1,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(x_0) + d_{F_{1,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(x_0) 
+ d_{M_2}(x_0) + d_{N_2}(x_0)\).
If there is no tracking \(T = x_0x_1\cdots x_{2k+2}\) in $\mathcal{B}$, where $x_0x_1$ is an 
edge of \(E(G)-E(G')\), then $\mathcal{B}(x_0)=0$. 
For every such tracking $T$, by the 
construction of $\mathcal{B}$, we know that $x_0x_1$ is an element of $S_{x_1}$.
Since \(x_1\) is a vertex of \(A_2\), we have 
that \(S_{x_1} \subset M_2\cup N_2 \cup F_{1,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits} \cup 
F_{1,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}\).
Therefore,
\begin{equation*}
\mathcal{B}(x_0) \leq d_{F_{1,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(x_0) + d_{F_{1,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(x_0) 
+ d_{M_2}(x_0) + d_{N_2}(x_0).
\end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Every end-edge at $x_0$ lies in an $S_{x_1}$, bounding $\mathcal{B}(x_0)$ above.
nodes.section: 6 Decomposition into paths of even length

nodes.name: Lower bound
nodes.statement:
Now we will prove that $\mathcal{B}(x_0)\geq d_{F_{1,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(x_0) + 
d_{F_{1,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(x_0) + d_{M_2}(x_0) + d_{N_2}(x_0)$.
Note that if \(x_0x_1\) is an edge of 
\(M_2\cup N_2 \cup F_{1,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits} \cup F_{1,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}\)
that is incident to \(x_0\) in $A_1$ \big(these are the only edges of $G$ that 
can contribute to $\mathcal{B}(x_0)$\big), then, by the construction of $\mathcal{B}$, there is a 
tracking \(Q' = x_1\cdots x_{2k+2}\) of a path such that the tracking  \(Q = x_0x_1\cdots 
x_{2k+2}\)\(x_0\) (of a vanilla trail) belongs to $\mathcal{B}$.
Therefore, \(\mathcal{B}(x_0) = d_{F_{1,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(x_0) + d_{F_{1,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}}(x_0) 
				+ d_{M_2}(x_0) + d_{N_2}(x_0)\).
nodes.statement_short: Every such edge is an end-edge of an extended tracking.
nodes.section: 6 Decomposition into paths of even length

nodes.name: Balance
nodes.statement:
Thus, for every vertex \(v\in A_1\) we have 
\begin{align*}
	\mathcal{B}(v)	&= |F_{1,2k}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}(v)| + |F_{1,2k+1}^{\mathop{\text{\rm forw}}\nolimits}(v)| + |M_2(v)| + 
|N_2(v)| \\
			&= 2d^*(v) + d_{M_2}(v) + d_{N_2}(v) \\
			&= d_{G_1}(v)/(2k+2) + d_{M_2}(v) + d_{N_2}(v).
\end{align*}
Analogously, we have \(\mathcal{B}(v) = d_{G_2}(v)/(2k+2) + d_{M_1}(v) + d_{N_1}(v)\)
for each vertex \(v\in A_2\).
Thus, \(\mathcal{B}\) is an \(\mathbb{F}\)-balanced vanilla $(2k+2)$-trail decomposition.
nodes.statement_short: Substitute $d^*$ to obtain the balance formula on both sides.

nodes.name: Extended decomposition is pre-complete (even case)
nodes.statement: \(\mathcal{B}\) is \((2k+3)\)-pre-complete.

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 6.9
nodes.statement:
Let  \(v\in A_i\).
We shall prove that \(\mathrm{preHang}(v,\mathcal{B}) > 2k+3\).
Note that, by the construction of $\mathcal{B}$, the set of pre-hanging edges at \(v\) 
in \(\mathcal{B}\)
is exactly \(S_v\).
Then, \(\mathrm{preHang}(v,\mathcal{B}) = |S_v| = \mathcal{B}'(v)\).
Since \(\mathcal{B}'\) is balanced, \(\mathcal{B}'(v) \geq d_{G'_i}(v)/(2k)\).
Therefore,
\begin{equation*}
	\mathrm{preHang}(v,\mathcal{B})	= \mathcal{B}'(v) 
					\geq d_{G'_i}(v)/(2k) 
					= 2d^*(v) 
					= d_{G_i}(v)/(2k+2).
\end{equation*} 
Since \(\mathbb{F}\) is a strong \(\big(2,2(2k+2)\big)\)-bifactorization of \(G\),
we have \(d_{G_i}(v) \geq (2k+2)(2k+4)\), from where we conclude that  
\(\mathrm{preHang}(v,\mathcal{B}) \geq 2k+4\).
Therefore, \(\mathcal{B}\) is a \((2k+3)\)-pre-complete vanilla trail decomposition.
nodes.statement_short: Pre-hanging edges at $v$ are exactly $S_v$, whose size is bounded below via balance and strongness.

in \(\mathcal{B}\)
is exactly \(S_v\).
Then, \(\mathrm{preHang}(v,\mathcal{B}) = |S_v| = \mathcal{B}'(v)\).
nodes.statement_short: Pre-hanging edges at $v$ are exactly $S_v$.

nodes.name: Lower bound
nodes.statement:
Since \(\mathcal{B}'\) is balanced, \(\mathcal{B}'(v) \geq d_{G'_i}(v)/(2k)\).
Therefore,
\begin{equation*}
	\mathrm{preHang}(v,\mathcal{B})	= \mathcal{B}'(v) 
					\geq d_{G'_i}(v)/(2k)

					= d_{G_i}(v)/(2k+2).

nodes.name: Strongness

Since \(\mathbb{F}\) is a strong \(\big(2,2(2k+2)\big)\)-bifactorization of \(G\),
we have \(d_{G_i}(v) \geq (2k+2)(2k+4)\), from where we conclude that  
\(\mathrm{preHang}(v,\mathcal{B}) \geq 2k+4\).
Therefore, \(\mathcal{B}\) is a \((2k+3)\)-pre-complete vanilla trail decomposition.
nodes.statement_short: Strongness gives the required bound.

nodes.name: Decomposition of highly edge-connected bipartite graphs into odd paths
nodes.statement:

\(G\) is a \(2(6k + 2r+1)\)-edge-connected bipartite graph such that \(|E(G)|\) 
is divisible by \(2k+1\),

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 7.1
nodes.statement:

nodes.name: Barát–Thomassen conjecture, version with 2|E(T)| dividing |E(G)|
nodes.section: 7.2 Paths of even length
nodes.label: conj:dec-bip2

nodes.name: Equivalence of the conjecture versions
nodes.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree with \(\ell\) edges, \(\ell \geq 3\). The following two statements are
equivalent.
\begin{itemize}
\item[(i)] There exists a positive integer $k''_T$ such that, if $G$ is a 
$k''_T$-edge-connected 
		bipartite graph and $2|E(T)|$ divides $|E(G)|$, then $G$ admits 
a $T$-decomposition.
\item[(ii)] There exists a positive integer $k'_T$ such that, if $G$ is a 
$k'_T$-edge-connected bipartite graph and $|E(T)|$ divides $|E(G)|$, then $G$ admits 
a 
$T$-decomposition.
\end{itemize}
	Furthermore, 
	\(
		k'_T\leq 2(k''_T + \ell).
	\)
assumptions: Let $T$ be a tree with \(\ell\) edges, \(\ell \geq 3\).
conclusions:
The following two statements are
equivalent.
equivalent_conditions:
There exists a positive integer $k''_T$ such that, if $G$ is a 
$k''_T$-edge-connected 
		bipartite graph and $2|E(T)|$ divides $|E(G)|$, then $G$ admits 
a $T$-decomposition

There exists a positive integer $k'_T$ such that, if $G$ is a 
$k'_T$-edge-connected bipartite graph and $|E(T)|$ divides $|E(G)|$, then $G$ admits 
a 
$T$-decomposition
nodes.statement_short: The conjectures with divisibility by $|E(T)|$ and by $2|E(T)|$ are equivalent, with $k'_T\le 2(k''_T+\ell)$.
nodes.section: 7.2 Paths of even length
nodes.label: theorem:conj-equivalence2

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 7.3
nodes.statement:
It suffices to prove that statement (i) implies statement (ii).
	Suppose statament (i) is true.
	Let \(G\) be an \(2(k''_T + \ell)\)-edge-connected graph such 
	that \(|E(G)|\) is divisible by \(\ell\).
	If \(|E(G)|\) is divisible by \(2\ell\),
	then \(G\) satisfies the conditions of statement (i),
	and therefore admits a \(T\)-decomposition.
	Thus, we may assume that \(|E(G)| = 2r\ell + \ell\) for some positive 
integer \(r\).
	 


	Clearly, \(G\) contains a copy \(T'\) of \(T\).
	By Theorem~\ref{thm:edge-disjoint-spanning-trees}, \(G\) contains at 
least
	\(k''_T + \ell\) edge-disjoint spanning trees.
	Since \(T'\) has \(\ell\) edges, \(T'\) intercepts at most \(\ell\) of 
	these spanning trees,
	and the graph \(G' = G - T'\) contains at least \(k''_T\) of 
these spanning trees.
	Thus, \(G'\) is \(k''_T\)-edge-connected.
	Note that \(|E(G')| = |E(G)| - \ell= 2r\ell\).
	By statement (i), \(G'\) admits a decomposition \(\mathcal{D}'\) into copies of 
\(T\).
	Thus, \(\mathcal{D} = \mathcal{D}' + T'\) is a decomposition of \(G\) into copies of 
\(T\).
nodes.statement_short: If $|E(G)|$ is an odd multiple of $\ell$, remove one copy of $T$; spanning-tree packing keeps the rest $k''_T$-edge-connected.
nodes.section: 7.2 Paths of even length

nodes.name: Reduce to (i)=>(ii)
nodes.statement:
It suffices to prove that statement (i) implies statement (ii).
	Suppose statament (i) is true.
nodes.statement_short: Only (i) implies (ii) needs proof.

Let \(G\) be an \(2(k''_T + \ell)\)-edge-connected graph such

Clearly, \(G\) contains a copy \(T'\) of \(T\).
	By Theorem~\ref{thm:edge-disjoint-spanning-trees}, \(G\) contains at

	\(k''_T + \ell\) edge-disjoint spanning trees.
	Since \(T'\) has \(\ell\) edges, \(T'\) intercepts at most \(\ell\) of

nodes.name: Apply (i)

\(T\).
